definition_zh: 害怕的；担心的；恐怕；不情愿的
definition_en: feeling fear, or worried, or sorry to say something
core_image: 孩子在黑屋子里靠近妈妈
scene: 停电的夜晚，小男孩待在妈妈身边不敢走开。 He is afraid of the dark.
sceneCN: 这里 afraid 是「害怕的」（第 1 个义项：感到恐惧）；句意为害怕黑暗。

pos.zh: 形容词：害怕的；担心的；恐怕；不情愿的

senses.title: Feeling fear
senses.definition: feeling fear about something
senses.definitionCN: 对某物感到恐惧
senses.example: The child is afraid of the dark.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子怕黑。
senses.why: Afraid is built from an old word for being frightened, so its first sense is plain fear.
senses.whyCN: afraid 由古英语表示「受惊」的词构成，第一义就是单纯的害怕。

senses.title: Worried about something
senses.definition: feeling worry that something bad may happen
senses.definitionCN: 担心可能发生不好的事
senses.example: I am afraid for her health.
senses.exampleCN: 我为她的健康担心。
senses.why: Fear pointed at what may happen becomes worry rather than terror.
senses.whyCN: 把害怕指向可能发生的不幸，就从惊恐变成担心。

senses.title: Used to soften bad news
senses.definition: used politely before bad or unwelcome news
senses.definitionCN: 在不好的消息前用作客气的开场
senses.example: I am afraid he is late.
senses.exampleCN: 恐怕他迟到了。
senses.why: The worry was softened into a polite opening, which is the sense of I am afraid.
senses.whyCN: 把担心弱化成客气的开场语，就是「恐怕」。

intro.en: The recorded history of afraid is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 afraid 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: The old word for a sudden danger or a fear gave the base.
items.cn: 古英语中表示突发危险或恐惧的词提供了基础。

items.en: Affray named a sudden disturbance or a fright.
items.cn: affray 指突发的骚动或惊吓。

items.en: The form affraid meant frightened.
items.cn: affraid 这一形式意为受惊的。

items.en: The spelling settled as afraid in modern English.
items.cn: 现代英语中拼写固定为 afraid。

items.en: Today it also serves as a polite way to say sorry.
items.cn: 今天它也用作礼貌地表示抱歉的说法。

note.en: The first group collects forms that look or sound alike; the second group collects words with a nearby meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收意义相近的词。

entries.definition: An old word for a fight or a disturbance.
entries.definitionCN: 指打斗或骚动的古词。

entries.definition: The common adjective for feeling fear.
entries.definitionCN: 表示感到害怕的常用形容词。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning full of fear.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为充满恐惧的。

entries.definition: A plain word for being afraid.
entries.definitionCN: 表示害怕的朴素说法。

entries.definition: It stresses thinking about a possible problem.
entries.definitionCN: 强调想着可能出现的问题。

entries.definition: It stresses being uneasy before an event.
entries.definitionCN: 强调事情发生前的紧张。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded form, the real family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的词形、真实的词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: The old word for fear gave afraid: to be afraid is to be in a state of fear.
normal.cn: 古词中表示恐惧的词给出了 afraid：be afraid 就是处在害怕的状态。

normal.en: The same family also gives fear and frightened.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 fear 与 frightened。

normal.en: It often appears in the phrase afraid of.
normal.cn: 它常出现在「害怕」这个搭配里。

normal.en: Spell it as it sounds: keep every letter of afraid in order.
normal.cn: 按读音拼写：把 afraid 的每个字母按顺序保留。

normal.en: Use it when you mean: feeling fear, or worried, or sorry to say something.
normal.cn: 当你想表达「害怕的」时用它。

abstract.en: Picture a child staying close to mother in a dark room.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子在黑屋子里靠近妈妈。

abstract.en: The same picture can be literal in one sentence and figurative in another.
abstract.cn: 同一幅画面在一句里可以是字面意思，在另一句里可以是比喻。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud first, then let the picture bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让画面把意思带回来。

examples.cn: 孩子怕黑。

examples.en: I am afraid for her health.

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of afraid grows from one core image: a child staying close to mother in a dark room.
sensesIntro.cn: afraid 的各个义项都从同一个核心意象生长出来：孩子在黑屋子里靠近妈妈。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a child staying close to mother in a dark room
core.cn: 核心意象：孩子在黑屋子里靠近妈妈

branches.en: Sense 01 covers the most literal use: Feeling fear.
branches.cn: 义项 01 覆盖最字面的用法：害怕。

branches.en: Sense 02 covers a wider everyday use: Worried about something.
branches.cn: 义项 02 覆盖更宽泛的日常用法：担心。

branches.en: Sense 03 covers a further use: Used to soften bad news.
branches.cn: 义项 03 覆盖更靠后的一种用法：恐怕。

branches.en: Sense 01 · 02 covers the two main uses: Feeling fear / Worried about something.
branches.cn: 义项 01 · 02 覆盖两个主要用法：害怕、担心。

branches.en: Sense 01 · 03 covers the two main uses: Feeling fear / Used to soften bad news.
branches.cn: 义项 01 · 03 覆盖两个主要用法：害怕、恐怕。

definition_zh: 铃；钟；铃声；钟形物
definition_en: a hollow metal object that rings when it is struck or shaken, or the sound it makes
core_image: 门边一枚小铜铃，被手指轻轻一碰就响
scene: 下课铃响了，走廊里一下子热闹起来。 The bell rang and the students ran out of the classroom.
sceneCN: 这里 bell 是「铃」（第 1 个义项：敲击或摇动会响的金属器物）；句意为铃响了，学生们跑出教室。

derivatives.zh: 由 door 与 bell 组合而成，义为「门铃」
由 bell 与 boy 组合而成，义为「酒店行李员」
由 bell 与 jar 组合而成，义为「钟罩」

senses.title: The ringing metal object
senses.definition: a hollow metal object, often shaped like a cup, that makes a clear sound when struck or shaken
senses.definitionCN: 一种中空金属器物，多呈杯状，被敲击或摇动时发出清脆声音
senses.example: The bell above the door was broken.
senses.exampleCN: 门上方的铃坏了。
senses.why: Old English belle named the ringing object, and the word itself looks like an imitation of the sound, so the object is the original sense.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 belle 就指这件会响的东西，词形本身像是在模仿那声响，所以「器物」义最原始。

senses.title: The sound itself
senses.definition: the sound made by a bell, especially as a signal
senses.definitionCN: 铃或钟发出的声音，尤指作为信号的那一声
senses.example: We heard the bell from the tower.
senses.exampleCN: 我们听见钟楼传来的钟声。
senses.why: The object and its sound are so closely tied that one word serves both, so bell can name the ringing as well as the metal that rings.
senses.whyCN: 器物与它的声音贴得太紧，一个词就同时承担两者，所以 bell 既能指那声响，也能指发声的金属。

senses.title: Something shaped like a bell
senses.definition: an object or shape that is wide at the bottom and narrow at the top, like a bell
senses.definitionCN: 下宽上窄、形状像钟的器物或轮廓
senses.example: Cover the young plant with a glass bell.
senses.exampleCN: 用玻璃钟罩把幼苗罩住。
senses.why: Because a bell has a wide skirt and a narrow top, anything with that outline borrowed the name, which is how the shape sense appeared.
senses.whyCN: 因为钟下摆宽、顶部窄，任何具有这个轮廓的东西都借用了这个名字，形状义就是这样产生的。

senses.title: To put a bell on
senses.definition: to attach a bell to an animal or an object
senses.definitionCN: 把铃系在动物或物体上
senses.example: The shepherd belled the lead goat.
senses.exampleCN: 牧人给领头羊系上了铃。
senses.why: The verb is simply the noun turned into action: putting the ringing object onto something so that its sound can be heard.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是名词转成动作：把会响的器物装到某物上，好让它的声音被听见。

intro.en: Bell is an old Germanic word that probably began as an imitation of the sound.
intro.cn: bell 是古老的日耳曼语词，最初很可能是在模仿那声响。

items.en: Old English belle named the ringing object, and the word looks like an imitation of its sound.
items.cn: 古英语 belle 指会响的器物，词形像是在模仿它发出的声音。

items.en: Dutch bel is a close relative, and both words seem to copy a ringing noise.
items.cn: 荷兰语 bel 是近亲，两个词似乎都在模仿叮当的响声。

items.en: The spelling settled as bell, and the meaning widened to any ringing metal object.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 bell，词义扩展到任何会响的金属器物。

items.en: Church bells marked the hours and called people together, which fixed the word in daily life.
items.cn: 教堂的钟用来报时和召集人，这把这个词牢牢固定在日常生活里。

items.en: Because a bell is wide at the bottom and narrow at the top, the word spread to anything of that shape.
items.cn: 因为钟下宽上窄，这个词扩展到了任何这种形状的东西。

items.en: Today bell covers doorbells, handbells, bell towers, and bell-shaped covers.
items.cn: 今天 bell 可指门铃、手铃、钟楼以及钟形罩。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that sound almost the same; the near-meaning group collects other things that ring or warn.
note.cn: 形近组收读音几乎相同的词；近义组收其他会响或用来示警的东西。

entries.definition: A beautiful woman or the most popular girl, pronounced exactly like bell.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「美女、交际花」，读音与 bell 完全相同。

entries.definition: The front part of the body below the chest.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「肚子、腹部」，开头读音相同。

entries.definition: A strip worn around the waist, or a band of material.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「腰带、带状物」，开头读音相同。

entries.definition: To shout very loudly and deeply.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「大声吼叫」，开头读音相同。

entries.definition: A set of bells, or the musical sound they make.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「编钟、一套钟」，也指它们奏出的乐声。

entries.definition: A large metal disc that rings when struck.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「锣」，一种敲击会响的大金属盘。

entries.definition: An electric device that makes a buzzing signal sound.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蜂鸣器」，一种发出嗡嗡信号的电器。

entries.definition: A sound or device that warns people of danger.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「警报」，用来提醒危险的声音或装置。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded Germanic origin, the real compounds, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的日耳曼语来源、真实复合词和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Old English belle probably copied the ringing sound, so the word sounds like what it names.
normal.cn: 古英语 belle 很可能是在模仿铃声，所以这个词读起来就像它所指的声音。

normal.en: Dutch bel is a cousin with the same ringing sense.
normal.cn: 荷兰语 bel 是同源近亲，也指会响的铃。

normal.en: Doorbell, bellboy and bell jar all keep the bell picture.
normal.cn: doorbell、bellboy、bell jar 都保留了「铃、钟」的画面。

normal.en: It commonly pairs with ring, door, alarm and tower.
normal.cn: 它常与 ring、door、alarm、tower 搭配。

normal.en: Spell b-e-l-l with a double l at the end, like two bells side by side.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-e-l-l，末尾两个 l 并排，像两只并排的铃。

abstract.en: See a small brass bell by a door and a finger about to touch it: that is bell.
abstract.cn: 想象门边一枚小铜铃，手指正要碰上去，那就是 bell。

abstract.en: Turn the same shape upside down onto a plant: the object becomes a cover, and the shape sense follows.
abstract.cn: 把同一个形状倒扣到植物上：器物变成罩子，形状义随之而来。

abstract.en: Say the word, then let the sound and the metal come back together.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让声音和金属一起回到脑海里。

examples.en: The bell rang and the students ran out of the classroom.
examples.cn: 铃响了，学生们跑出教室。

examples.en: The bell above the door was broken.
examples.cn: 门上方的铃坏了。

examples.en: We heard the bell from the tower.
examples.cn: 我们听见钟楼传来的钟声。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「贝尔」——贝尔发明的电话一响，就像铃在叫：铃

root: bell 来自古英语 belle，很可能是在模仿铃响的声音，荷兰语 bel 与它同源。这个词最初指会响的金属器物，随后也指它发出的声音；因为它下宽上窄，又引申出「钟形物」；名词转动词后表示「给……系铃」。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of bell come from one small metal object: the thing that rings, the ring it makes, the shape it has, and the act of putting it on.
sensesIntro.cn: bell 的四个义项都出自同一件小金属器物：会响的它、它发出的响、它的形状，以及把铃装上去的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small brass bell by a door, touched by a finger
core.cn: 核心意象：门边一枚小铜铃，被手指轻轻一碰

branches.en: THE OBJECT: the first sense is the hollow metal thing itself.
branches.cn: 器物线：第一个义项就是那件中空金属器物本身。

branches.en: THE SOUND: the same word also names the ringing it produces.
branches.cn: 声音线：同一个词也指它发出的那阵响。

branches.en: THE SHAPE: the wide skirt and narrow top turn into the bell-shaped cover.
branches.cn: 形状线：下摆宽、顶部窄，变成钟形的罩子。

branches.en: THE ACTION: the noun becomes a verb for putting a bell on something.
branches.cn: 动作线：名词转成动词，表示给某物系铃。

branches.en: THE TWO EXTENSIONS: sound and shape are the directions this small object grew in.
branches.cn: 两支线：声音与形状是这件小器物向外生长的两个方向。

intro.cn: bell 是基础名词，下面列出的是它的复数、真实复合词以及常与它搭配的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin campana and tintinnabulum are recorded words for bells; English took its word from Germanic, so these are parallels.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 campana 与 tintinnabulum 是有记录的「钟、铃」用词；英语这个词来自日耳曼语，因此二者只是平行词。

definition_zh: 很可能；大概；想必；多半
definition_en: used to say that something is very likely to be true or to happen, or to make a guess sound less certain
core_image: 云压得很低，出门前顺手拿起一把伞
scene: 窗外的云压得很低，风把晾着的衣服吹得直响，母亲在门口把伞塞进孩子书包。 It will probably rain before the children get home.
sceneCN: 这里的 probably 表示「很可能」（第 1 个义项：对将要发生的事作出高概率判断）；句意为在孩子们到家之前多半会下雨。图中可辨识物件：压低的云、被风吹起的衣服、塞进书包的伞。

derivatives.zh: 去掉副词词尾 -ly 得到的形容词，义为「很可能的；可信的」
由 probable 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「可能性；概率」
由否定前缀 im- 加 probable 构成，义为「不大可能的」

senses.title: Very likely to be true or to happen
senses.definition: used to say that something is more likely than not, though not certain
senses.definitionCN: 表示某事发生的可能性大于不发生的可能性，但并非确定
senses.example: The train will probably leave from platform three.
senses.exampleCN: 火车很可能会从三号站台开出。
senses.why: Latin probabilis described what could be proved or accepted, and the adverb keeps that measured confidence rather than absolute certainty.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 probabilis 形容能够被证明或接受的东西，副词保留的正是这种有分寸的把握，而不是绝对的确定。

senses.title: Judging from the evidence, almost certainly
senses.definition: used when the facts already known point strongly to one conclusion
senses.definitionCN: 在已知事实强烈指向某个结论时使用
senses.example: She has not answered for two days, so she is probably away.
senses.exampleCN: 她两天没回音，想必是不在。
senses.why: When the likelihood rests on evidence rather than on hope, the same adverb shifts from prediction to inference about what has already happened.
senses.whyCN: 当这种可能性建立在证据而不是愿望上，同一个副词就从预测将来转到推断已经发生的事。

senses.title: Used to soften a guess about other people
senses.definition: used politely to avoid sounding too sure about another person's situation or reasons
senses.definitionCN: 礼貌地避免对别人的处境或理由显得过于肯定
senses.example: You probably have your own reasons for saying nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 你大概有自己的理由不开口。
senses.why: Saying probably hands part of the judgement back to the listener, which is why the word so often appears when a speaker wants to be tactful.
senses.whyCN: 说出 probably 等于把一部分判断交回给听者，所以说话人想留面子时，这个词特别常出现。

intro.en: Probably belongs to a Latin family of testing and proving: what is probable is what can stand up to examination.
intro.cn: probably 属于拉丁语中检验、证明这一族词：probable 就是经得起检验的东西。

items.en: Probus meant upright, honest, and sound, said of a person or a thing that could be trusted without further proof.
items.cn: probus 意为正直、诚实、可靠，用来形容不必再验证就可信任的人或物。

items.en: The verb probare meant to test, to examine, and to show that something is good; English prove and probe descend from it.
items.cn: 动词 probare 意为检验、考察、证明某物是好的；英语的 prove 与 probe 都由它而来。

items.en: Probabilis meant able to be approved or accepted, a claim that could pass the test, and it is the direct source of the English adjective.
items.cn: probabilis 意为能够被认可或接受的，即经得起检验的主张，是英语形容词的直接来源。

items.en: Old French borrowed the adjective as probable, meaning credible or likely, and Middle English took it over in the same shape.
items.cn: 古法语借入这个形容词写作 probable，意为可信的、很可能的，中古英语原样接收。

items.en: The adverb probably was formed with -ly and settled into its modern sense of very likely; earlier English used it more narrowly for what could be proved.
items.cn: 副词 probably 由 -ly 构成，最终固定为很可能的现代义；早期英语用它时范围更窄，专指能够被证明的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin stem prob- and its English shapes; the near-meaning group gathers the other adverbs English uses to hedge a claim.
note.cn: 形近组沿拉丁词干 prob- 及英语词形展开；近义组收英语里其他用来给判断留余地的副词。

entries.definition: Likely to be true or to happen; the adjective behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 很可能为真或发生的；副词背后的形容词。

entries.definition: How likely something is, often expressed as a number.
entries.definitionCN: 某事发生的可能程度，常用数字表示。

entries.definition: Not likely to happen or be true.
entries.definitionCN: 不大可能发生或为真的。

entries.definition: A period of testing a person's behaviour, from the same verb probare.
entries.definitionCN: 考察某人表现的一段时间，出自同一个动词 probare。

entries.definition: Used to say something may be true, with less confidence than probably.
entries.definitionCN: 表示某事可能为真，把握比 probably 小。

entries.definition: Used when something can happen, even if it is not likely.
entries.definitionCN: 表示某事有可能发生，即使可能性不大。

entries.definition: Expected to happen; the adjective and adverb closest in force to this word.
entries.definitionCN: 预期会发生的；语气上最接近这个词的形容词与副词。

entries.definition: Used when a conclusion is taken as true because nothing suggests otherwise.
entries.definitionCN: 在没有相反迹象时把某个结论当作成立地使用。

normalIntro.en: The word comes from a Latin verb of testing, so probably does not mean certain but has passed enough tests to be believed.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词出自拉丁语中表示检验的动词，所以 probably 不是确定，而是已经通过足够检验、可以相信。

normal.en: Probare means to test, and English prove comes from the same verb, so probable and provable began close together.
normal.cn: probare 意为检验，英语 prove 同出这一动词，所以 probable 与 provable 最初挨得很近。

normal.en: Probabilis added -bilis, the ending that means able to be, as in visible and possible.
normal.cn: probabilis 加了 -bilis，这个词尾意为能够被，和 visible、possible 里的一样。

normal.en: Probably is the adjective probable plus -ly, the standard English path from adjective to adverb.
normal.cn: probably 是形容词 probable 加 -ly，这是英语从形容词到副词的标准路径。

normal.en: Most probably and quite probably stack a degree word in front, because likelihood comes in levels.
normal.cn: most probably 与 quite probably 在前面加程度词，因为可能性是分档的。

normal.en: Improbable flips the judgement with im-, the same negative prefix as in impossible.
normal.cn: improbable 用 im- 把判断翻过来，和 impossible 里的否定前缀一样。

abstract.en: A word from the courtroom of proof ended up as the everyday adverb of guesswork, which shows how much of proof is just expectation.
abstract.cn: 一个出自证明的词，最后成了日常推测的副词，说明证明里有很大一部分不过是对结果的预期。

abstract.en: Probably never claims certainty; it measures the distance between what we know and what we say.
abstract.cn: probably 从不声称确定；它量的是我们知道多少与说出多少之间的距离。

abstract.en: Every forecast is a small bet, and this adverb is the polite way of naming the odds without handing over the money.
abstract.cn: 每一次预报都是一笔小赌注，这个副词就是礼貌地点出赔率、却不把押金交出去的方式。

examples.en: The train will probably leave from platform three.
examples.cn: 火车很可能会从三号站台开出。

examples.en: She has not answered for two days, so she is probably away.
examples.cn: 她两天没回音，想必是不在。

examples.en: It will probably rain before you reach the station.
examples.cn: 在你到车站之前多半会下雨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「普若巴巴利」——十有八九，嘴上还要留一点余地，就是 probably。

root: 拉丁语 probus（正直可靠的）→ probare（检验、证明）→ probabilis（经得起检验的、可信的）→ 古法语 probable → 中古英语 probable → 加 -ly 成 probably。同族还有 prove、probe、probability、probation。

sensesIntro.en: The core is tested likelihood; the senses divide by what the likelihood rests on — plain prediction, evidence already in hand, or politeness toward the listener.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是经过检验的可能性；义项按可能性的依据分开：单纯的预测、手里已有的证据，或对听者的客气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: low clouds and a hand reaching for an umbrella.
core.cn: 核心意象：云压得很低，一只手顺手拿起了伞。

branches.en: an umbrella taken on a cloudy errand
branches.cn: 阴云下出门顺手带上的伞

branches.en: an empty chair and two days of silence
branches.cn: 两天没有回音和一把空椅子

branches.en: a pause before telling someone your guess
branches.cn: 说出猜测前的那一顿

branches.en: the same caution, once about facts and once about feelings
branches.cn: 同一种谨慎，一次对事实，一次对人心

branches.en: the odds named without a promise
branches.cn: 只报赔率、不作保证的同一句话

intro.en: The word is a Latin adjective of proof with two English endings on top; the eight entries trace test, proof, likelihood and the adverb itself.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中表示证明的形容词加上两层英语词尾；下面八条依次走过检验、证明、可能性与副词本身。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb probare and the adjective probabilis are both recorded, so the English family rests on attested forms rather than on guesswork.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语动词 probare 与形容词 probabilis 都有记录，所以这族英语词建立在有据可查的形式上，而不是猜测。

items.meaning: able to be proved or accepted

definition_zh: 财富；大量钱财与资产；也指丰富、充裕
definition_en: a large amount of money, property and other valuable assets; also an abundance of something valuable
core_image: 一间库房堆着金条、地契与粮袋，角落里还立着一架书，物质与精神都显得充足
scene: 老人把一生的积蓄、房产与藏书都写进同一份清单。 The family's wealth grew from land and trade rather than from wages.
sceneCN: 此处指「大量钱财与资产」（第 1 个义项：可估价的财富总量）；句意为这家人的财富来自土地与贸易，而非工资。图中可辨识物件：金条、地契、粮袋、书架。

pos.zh: 丰富；大量（用于表示「大量……」的固定结构）

forms.label: 复数（罕见，指多种财富形态）

senses.title: A large amount of money and assets
senses.definition: a great quantity of money, property, investments and other valuable things owned by a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 个人或群体拥有的大量金钱、房产、投资及其他贵重物品
senses.example: Her wealth came from shares in the family firm.
senses.exampleCN: 她的财富来自家族企业的股份。
senses.why: The word names a large store of what people value, so its first sense is simply the quantity of money and goods held.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是人们所看重之物的大量积蓄，因此第一义就是所持金钱与物品的数量。

senses.title: Total net assets of a person or group
senses.titleCN: 个人或群体的净资产总额
senses.definition: the total value of assets minus debts, viewed as a stock at a point in time
senses.definitionCN: 资产总值减去负债，作为某一时点的存量看待
senses.example: The survey measures household wealth as assets minus mortgage debt.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查把家庭财富算作资产减去房贷。
senses.why: Accounting turns a pile of possessions into a single net figure, which is the technical stock sense.
senses.whyCN: 会计把一堆财物变成一个净值数字，这就是技术性的存量义。

senses.title: Valuable natural resources
senses.definition: minerals, fertile land, water, forests and other natural endowments that a place possesses
senses.definitionCN: 一个地方拥有的矿产、沃土、水源、森林等自然禀赋
senses.example: The region's wealth lay in its forests and rivers.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的财富在于森林与河流。
senses.why: A country can be rich without money in banks, because land and resources are also stores of value.
senses.whyCN: 一个国家可以没有银行存款仍然富足，因为土地与资源也是价值储备。

senses.title: Prosperity and wellbeing
senses.definition: the older sense of a good and flourishing condition, close to welfare rather than to money alone
senses.definitionCN: 较古的义项，指良好兴旺的处境，接近福祉而非单指金钱
senses.example: The old prayer asked for health and wealth for the household.
senses.exampleCN: 古老的祷词为全家祈求健康与兴旺。
senses.why: Before it meant money, the word meant a good state of life, and that older flourishing sense still colours religious and ceremonial use.
senses.whyCN: 在指金钱之前，这个词指良好的生活状态，这一较古的兴旺义仍影响宗教与仪式用语。

senses.title: An abundance of a thing
senses.definition: a large supply or great amount of something, as in a wealth of detail or experience
senses.definitionCN: 某物的大量供应，如大量细节或丰富经验
senses.example: The archive offers a wealth of detail about daily life.
senses.exampleCN: 这座档案馆提供了关于日常生活的丰富细节。
senses.why: Abundance of money and abundance of anything share the same shape, so the word extends to non-material plenty.
senses.whyCN: 钱财的充裕与任何东西的充裕形状相同，因此这个词扩展到非物质的丰富。

senses.title: The collective riches of a society
senses.definition: the total stock of valuable assets held by a whole society or economy
senses.definitionCN: 整个社会或经济所持有的有价值资产总量
senses.example: Economists study how wealth is distributed across the country.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家研究财富在全国如何分布。
senses.why: Once the word is applied to a whole society, it names an aggregate stock rather than one person's fortune.
senses.whyCN: 这个词一旦用于整个社会，命名的就是总存量，而非某个人的财产。

senses.title: Inherited or accumulated stock
senses.definition: riches passed down or built up over time rather than earned in a single transaction
senses.definitionCN: 经继承或长期积累而非一次交易所得的钱财
senses.example: Much of the family's wealth had been inherited from two generations back.
senses.exampleCN: 这家的财富很多是两代之前继承下来的。
senses.why: Wealth accumulates, so it often carries the idea of a stock built or handed down across time.
senses.whyCN: 财富会累积，因此常带有跨时间积累或传下的存量意味。

senses.title: The common good in older usage
senses.definition: the public good or general wellbeing of a community, preserved in the compound commonweal
senses.definitionCN: 共同体的公共利益或整体福祉，保留在「公共福祉」这一复合词中
senses.example: Old writers spoke of the wealth of the realm as its common good.
senses.exampleCN: 古代作者把国家的财富说成公共之善。
senses.why: The oldest sense tied riches to the health of a community, and traces of it survive in formal and historical language.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项把财富与共同体的健全相连，其痕迹仍留在正式与历史语体中。

intro.en: Wealth is native English, built from an Old English noun for wellbeing with an abstract suffix. It has no Latin ancestor and dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 财富是英语本族词，由古英语中表示安好的名词加抽象后缀构成。它没有拉丁语祖先，年代均为约数。

items.en: Wela meant 'wellbeing, prosperity, riches' and was related to the word for 'well'. It described a good condition before it described money.
items.cn: wela 意为「安好、兴旺、财富」，与表示「好」的词同源。它先描述良好处境，后描述钱财。

items.en: The abstract suffix -th turned wela into welth, the state of being well-off, in the Middle English period.
items.cn: 抽象后缀把 wela 变成 welth，即「富足的状态」，时在中古英语时期。

items.en: By the modern period the material sense of money and property dominated, while the older wellbeing sense survived mainly in compounds and religious language.
items.cn: 到近现代，金钱与财产的物质义占据主导，较古的安好义主要保存在复合词与宗教语言里。

items.en: The phrase a wealth of extended the word from money to any large supply, such as detail, experience or evidence.
items.cn: 「大量的」这一说法把词义从金钱扩展到任何大量供应，如细节、经验或证据。

items.en: Economics fixed wealth as a stock of assets held at a point in time, in contrast with income as a flow.
items.cn: 经济学把财富固定为某一时点的资产存量，与作为流量的收入相对。

items.en: Attestation uncertain (first citation of the material sense): the transition from wellbeing to money is gradual and no single first use is recorded.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定（物质义的）：从安好到金钱的转变是渐进的，没有单一的最早用例。

note.en: Group one separates near neighbours that are often mistaken for relatives; group two holds words for large possessions.
note.cn: 第一组区分常被误认作同族的近邻词；第二组是表示大量财物的词。

entries.definition: Health comes from Old English hælþ 'wholeness' and is related to whole, not to wela; the shared ending is deceptive.
entries.definitionCN: 健康来自古英语 hælþ「完整」，与「完整」一词同源，与财富的词根无关；相同的词尾容易误导。

entries.definition: Welfare joins 'well' with 'fare' meaning journey or condition; it is a separate compound, not a derivative of wealth.
entries.definitionCN: 福利由「好」与「行程、处境」合成，是另一个复合词，并非财富的派生词。

entries.definition: Commonwealth is common plus wealth, naming a political community that shares a common good; it is a relative but not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 联邦由「共同」加「财富」构成，指共享公共之善的政治共同体；它是同族词，却不是同义词。

entries.definition: Weal is the older noun for wellbeing from which wealth was built, and it survives mainly in set phrases.
entries.definitionCN: weal 是构成财富的较古名词，意为安好，主要保留在固定说法里。

entries.definition: Riches is a plural noun for abundant valuable possessions, often used figuratively for richness of experience.
entries.definitionCN: riches 是表示大量贵重财物的复数名词，也常比喻经验的丰富。

entries.definition: Fortune is a very large amount of money owned by one person or family, close to the personal sense of wealth.
entries.definitionCN: fortune 指个人或家庭拥有的大笔钱财，接近财富的个人义。

entries.definition: Assets are the items of value on a balance sheet, the accounting parts from which net wealth is calculated.
entries.definitionCN: 资产是资产负债表上有价值的项目，是计算净财富的会计组成部分。

entries.definition: Affluence stresses a high level of consumption and goods rather than the stock of assets itself.
entries.definitionCN: 富裕强调高水平的消费与商品，而不是资产存量本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real native root, real compounds and real accounting phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的本族词根、真实的复合词与真实的会计说法。

normal.en: The root meant wellbeing before it meant money, so the older sense still echoes in formal language.
normal.cn: 词根先指安好，后指钱财，因此较古的义项仍在正式语体中回响。

normal.en: The abstract ending turns an adjective of goodness into the state of being well-off.
normal.cn: 抽象后缀把表示「好」的形容词变成「富足的状态」。

normal.en: A wealth of detail and a wealth of money share the same shape: a large supply.
normal.cn: 大量细节与大量金钱形状相同：都是一种充裕的供应。

normal.en: Economics keeps wealth as a stock and income as a flow, and the two should not be swapped.
normal.cn: 经济学把财富当存量、收入当流量，两者不能互换。

normal.en: The older public-good sense survives in the compound for a political community.
normal.cn: 较古的公共之善义保留在指政治共同体的复合词里。

abstract.en: Picture a storehouse where gold, grain and books sit on the same shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象一间库房，金条、粮食与书摆在同一层架上。

abstract.en: Picture a river that keeps flowing while a reservoir holds its water still.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河不断流动，而水库把水静静存住。

abstract.en: Picture a society whose common good is written on a shared ledger.
abstract.cn: 想象一个社会，把公共之善记在一本共同的账上。

examples.en: The country's wealth is concentrated in a few coastal cities.
examples.cn: 这个国家的财富集中在少数沿海城市。

examples.en: She brought a wealth of experience to the negotiation.
examples.cn: 她为谈判带来了丰富的经验。

examples.en: Wealth can grow while wages stay flat, which widens the gap between owners and workers.
examples.cn: 财富可以在工资停滞时增长，从而扩大所有者与劳动者之间的差距。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「围」加「思」——把金条、地契与粮食围起来反复思量，就是财富；联想「围起来的家底」

root: 古英语 wela「安好、兴旺、财富」加抽象后缀构成，属日耳曼语本族词，没有拉丁语来源；其较古义为良好处境，后收窄为钱财与资产，并保留「大量、丰富」的引申义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one store of value: money and assets are added into a net stock, extended to land, to prosperity, to any abundance, to a society's total and finally to the common good.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一份价值储存展开：钱财与资产先被加成净值，再扩展到土地、兴旺、任何充裕、社会总量，最后到公共之善。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a storehouse holding gold, deeds, grain and books on the same shelves.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间库房，金条、地契、粮袋与书都摆在同一层架上。

branches.en: THE STORE: possessions are first counted, then reduced to a net stock.
branches.cn: 储存：财物先被清点，再折算成净存量。

branches.en: THE LAND: value also lies in rivers, forests and minerals.
branches.cn: 土地：价值也藏在河流、森林与矿藏里。

branches.en: THE GOOD STATE: the oldest sense is flourishing life, not coin.
branches.cn: 良好状态：最古老的义项是兴旺的生活，而不是钱币。

branches.en: ABUNDANCE AND AGGREGATE: any large supply, and the whole society's total, share the same shape.
branches.cn: 充裕与总量：任何大量供应与整个社会的总量，形状相同。

branches.en: TIME AND THE COMMON: what is handed down, and what is held in common.
branches.cn: 时间与公共：一边是传下的存量，一边是共同持有的福祉。

intro.en: Wealth and its relatives are native English; no Latin source is involved, so the family is read from Old English alone.
intro.cn: 财富及其同族词是英语本族词，不涉及拉丁语来源，因此这个词族只能从古英语读起。

latinIntro.en: There are no Latin entries for this word: the root is Germanic and the suffixes are native or French-influenced.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语条目：词根是日耳曼语，后缀为本族或受法语影响的形式。

items.example: The wealthy district built its own school.
items.exampleCN: 这个富裕城区自建了一所学校。

items.example: The coast grew wealthier than the interior.
The wealthiest families owned most of the land.
items.exampleCN: 最富有的家族拥有大部分土地。

items.example: Old texts wished the town weal.
The commonweal was invoked in the debate.
items.exampleCN: 辩论中援引了公共福祉。

items.example: The scheme worked well for small farms.
items.exampleCN: 这项计划对小农场很有效。

definition_zh: 过去；往昔；过去的；以前的；经过；超过
definition_en: the time before now; belonging to an earlier time; moving from one side of something to the other; later than or beyond a point
core_image: 身后一条已经走完的路，脚印还在，前面的路还没踩出来
scene: 老屋的墙上挂着一排褪色的照片，屋里的人坐在灯下翻看从前的日子。 He rarely talks about his past, even with close friends.
sceneCN: 这里是「过去、往昔」（第 1 个义项：已经发生的时间）；句意是他很少谈起自己的过去，对亲近的朋友也一样。画面里有旧照片、台灯和翻动相册的手。

derivatives.zh: 由 past 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「已成为过去的状态」
由 past 与 due 复合而成，义为「逾期的；过期的」
由 past 与 master 复合而成，义为「老手；行家」

senses.title: The time before now
senses.definition: the time that has already happened, considered as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 已经发生过的全部时间，作为整体来看
senses.example: The village has changed a great deal in the past.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子在过去发生了很大变化。
senses.why: Past began as the participle of the verb meaning to go by, and what has gone by is exactly what we call the past.
senses.whyCN: past 原本是表示「走过去」的动词的分词，凡是已经走过去的，正是一段时间意义上的「过去」。

senses.title: Gone by; belonging to an earlier time
senses.definition: describing something that existed or happened before now and is no longer as it was
senses.definitionCN: 描述在此刻之前存在或发生、如今已不再是原样的东西
senses.example: She met an old friend and they talked about past summers.
senses.exampleCN: 她遇到一位老朋友，两人聊起从前的夏天。
senses.why: Once the participle describes time that has gone by, it can stand before a noun and mark that thing as belonging to the gone-by time.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个分词用来描述「已经走过去的时间」，它就能放在名词前，把那件事物标成属于那段过去的时光。

senses.title: Beyond a point in space
senses.definition: moving from one side of a place or object to the other, and ending up beyond it
senses.definitionCN: 从某地或某物的一侧移到另一侧，最后落在它的那一边
senses.example: A bus went past the school without stopping.
senses.exampleCN: 一辆公交车经过学校却没有停。
senses.why: The idea of going by turns into a preposition of place: you move along the side and leave the point behind you.
senses.whyCN: 「从旁边走过去」这个意思后来变成表示位置的介词：你沿着旁边移动，把那个点留在身后。

senses.title: Later than a stated time or beyond a limit
senses.definition: later than a particular hour, or more than a particular amount or stage
senses.definitionCN: 晚于某个时刻，或多于某个数量、越过某个阶段
senses.example: It was past midnight when the last guest left.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一位客人离开时已经过了午夜。
senses.why: If you have walked past a mark on a road, you are now beyond it; applied to hours and numbers, the same picture gives the sense of exceeding a limit.
senses.whyCN: 如果你已经走过路上的某个标记，你就到了它之外；把这一画面用到钟点和数字上，就得到「超过某个界限」的意思。

intro.en: Past is the old participle of pass, so its history is the history of walking by, worn down into a word for time that has walked away.
intro.cn: past 是 pass 旧时的分词，它的历史就是「从旁边走过」的历史，最后磨成一个指「已经走掉的时间」的词。

items.en: Passus was a step or a pace, and it named the distance a foot could cover at one stride.
items.cn: passus 意为一步、一步的距离，指一只脚迈一次所跨过的长度。

items.en: The verb passare grew from that noun and meant to step, to go through or to go by.
items.cn: 动词 passare 由这个名词发展而来，意为迈步、穿过、从旁经过。

items.en: Old French passer carried the verb into everyday use, and its past participle passé meant gone by.
items.cn: 古法语 passer 把这个动词带入日常使用，它的过去分词 passé 意为「已经过去的」。

items.en: English took past from that participle, first as a form of the verb pass and then as an adjective and a noun.
items.cn: 英语从这一分词借入 past，先作动词 pass 的一种形式，随后作形容词和名词。

items.en: Modern English adds the prepositional uses, the grammatical term past tense, and the fixed phrase in the past.
items.cn: 现代英语又添出介词的用法、语法术语「过去时」，以及固定说法 in the past。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers relatives of the verb pass, including the French borrowing that gave English its participle; the near-meaning group gathers words for earlier time.
note.cn: 形近组收的是动词 pass 的同族词，包括把分词送给英语的那个法语借词；近义组收的是表示「较早时间」的词。

entries.definition: To go by, to move beyond, or to hand something over.
entries.definitionCN: 经过；越过；也指把东西递过去。

entries.definition: A way through, or a stretch of text or music.
entries.definitionCN: 通道；也指一段文字或音乐。

entries.definition: Someone who happens to walk past a place.
entries.definitionCN: 恰好从某处走过的路人。

entries.definition: No longer in fashion; dated.
entries.definitionCN: 过时的；不再时兴的。

entries.definition: Belonging to an earlier time or to a previous state.
entries.definitionCN: 属于较早时期或先前状态的；以前的。

entries.definition: Coming before the one mentioned or the present one.
entries.definitionCN: 在提到的那一个或现在这个之前的。

entries.definition: Belonging to a time that has gone, often used of days or years.
entries.definitionCN: 属于已逝时光的，常用于 days 或 years。

normalIntro.en: The word is a participle that learned to stand alone, so every sense still carries the small movement of walking by.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词本是一个学会独立站立的分词，所以每个义项里都还带着「从旁边走过去」的小动作。

normal.en: Past is the participle of pass: time that has passed is the past.
normal.cn: past 是 pass 的分词：已经过去的时间，就是 the past。

normal.en: Walk past a shop and you leave it behind, which is why the preposition means beyond.
normal.cn: 从一家店前走过，就把它留在身后，这就是这个介词表示「越过」的原因。

normal.en: Half past ten means the hour hand has walked past the ten mark.
normal.cn: half past ten 意为时针已经走过了十点那个刻度。

normal.en: The past tense is the verb form used for what has already happened.
normal.cn: 过去时是用来表示已经发生之事的动词形式。

normal.en: As a noun it takes a regular plural, pasts, when several different pasts are compared.
normal.cn: 作名词比较几种不同的过去时，复数按规则写作 pasts。

abstract.en: The past is not a place you can visit, only a direction you have already walked.
abstract.cn: 过去不是能去的地方，只是你已经走过的一个方向。

abstract.en: English uses one small word for time gone and space passed, hinting that memory and motion share a shape.
abstract.cn: 英语用同一个小词表示逝去的时间与走过的空间，暗示记忆与移动共享同一种形状。

abstract.en: To say something is past is to say the road behind you no longer pulls at your feet.
abstract.cn: 说某件事已经过去，等于说身后那条路不再拽着你的脚。

examples.en: The past is never as simple as it looks from here.
examples.cn: 过去从来不像从这里看上去那样简单。

examples.en: We drove past the old mill on the way home.
examples.cn: 回家的路上我们开车经过了那座老磨坊。

examples.en: It is half past nine, so the shop is already open.
examples.cn: 现在九点半，商店已经开门了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕斯特」——想起过去的事有点怕；past 就是过去。

root: 由古法语 passer 的过去分词 passé 演变而来，源头是拉丁语 passus（一步）与晚期拉丁语 passare（通过）。

sensesIntro.en: The core is movement that leaves a point behind; time that has left us becomes the noun, and space left behind becomes the preposition.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把某个点留在身后」的移动；离开我们的时间成了名词，被留在身后的空间成了介词。

branches.en: a bus sliding by a school gate without stopping
branches.cn: 一辆公交车驶过校门没有停

branches.cn: 指针已经把午夜留在身后的钟

definition_en: a series of pictures in the mind during sleep, or a strong hope for the future
core_image: 闭眼后脑海里放起的无声电影
scene: 午休的教室里，他把脸埋进臂弯，梦里已是世界杯的决赛场。 He had a strange dream about flying last night.

dream 加形容词后缀构成，义为「梦幻般的；恍惚的」

senses.title: Pictures in the mind during sleep
senses.definition: images and events in the mind while sleeping
senses.definitionCN: 睡眠时脑中出现的图像与情景
senses.example: I had a dream that I was swimming.
senses.exampleCN: 我梦见自己在游泳。
senses.why: Old English dream first meant joyful noise; the sleeping pictures took over the word later.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 dream 最初指欢快的声响；后来睡眠中的画面接管了这个词。

senses.title: A strong hope for the future
senses.definition: something you strongly wish to achieve
senses.definitionCN: 非常渴望实现的事
senses.example: Her dream is to become a doctor.
senses.exampleCN: 她的梦想是成为一名医生。
senses.why: Sleeping pictures are wishes that feel real, so waking hopes borrowed the same word.
senses.whyCN: 睡梦中的画面逼真得像愿望成真，于是醒着的希望借用了同一个词。

senses.title: To imagine or wish idly
senses.definition: to let the mind wander to pleasant fancies
senses.definitionCN: 任思绪漂向美好的幻想
senses.example: He sat dreaming of the summer sea.
senses.exampleCN: 他坐着幻想夏日的海。
senses.why: The mind plays its own film when the eyes do nothing.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛闲着时，心里自会放映它的电影。

intro.en: Dream began as a sound of joy, and only later became the film in your sleep.
intro.cn: dream 起初是欢乐之声，后来才变成你睡梦中的电影。

items.en: Old English dream meant joy, mirth, music making.
items.cn: 古英语 dream 意为欢乐、喜庆、奏乐。

items.en: Norse draumr meant a sleeping dream, closely related in form.
items.cn: 诺斯语 draumr 意为睡眠之梦，形式上 closely related。

items.en: The sleeping sense, helped by Norse, replaced the joy sense.
items.cn: 在诺斯语的助推下，睡眠义取代了欢乐义。

items.en: Dream came to name both night visions and day hopes.
items.cn: dream 开始兼指夜间幻象与白日的希望。

items.en: Modern English keeps noun and verb side by side.
items.cn: 现代英语保留其名词与动词用法。

note.en: These words sit near dream in form or meaning.
note.cn: 这些词在形式或意义上与 dream 相邻。

entries.definition: great fear, different root

entries.definitionCN: 幻象；憧憬

normalIntro.cn: 用「脑中无声电影」的画面和 dream 词族来记。

normal.en: dream of means wish for or see in sleep.

normal.en: A dream job pays and pleases at once.

abstract.en: See clouds rolling under your bare feet.
abstract.cn: 看云海从赤脚下翻滚而过。

abstract.en: Hear the quiet of a sleeping town.
abstract.cn: 听沉睡小镇的寂静。

abstract.en: Feel the lightness of floating above your street.
abstract.cn: 感受飘在街道上空的轻盈。

examples.en: Last night I dreamed that our team won the cup.
examples.cn: 昨晚我梦见我们队夺了杯。

examples.en: Keep working and your dream will come true.
examples.cn: 坚持下去，你的梦想终会实现。

examples.en: She dreams of opening a small bakery.
examples.cn: 她梦想开一家小面包店。

branches.cn: 从睡眠画面到人生目标

definition_zh: 相信；认为；信仰；信任
definition_en: to accept that something is true, or to have confidence in someone
core_image: 一个人把手里的一封信交给另一个人，对方点头收下
scene: 雨天的车站里，陌生人说下一班车还会来，女孩选择相信他。 The girl believed the stranger and waited for the next bus.
sceneCN: 这里 believe 是「相信（某人的话）」（第 1 个义项：认为某说法是真的）；句意为女孩相信了陌生人，等着下一班车。

pos.zh: 动词：相信；认为；信仰；信任

derivatives.zh: 由 believe 的词干加 -f 构成，义为「信念；相信」
由 believe 加 -er 构成，义为「信徒；相信的人」
由 believe 加 -able 构成，义为「可信的」
由 un- 加 believable 构成，义为「难以置信的」

senses.title: To accept something as true
senses.definition: to accept that a statement, report, or idea is true
senses.definitionCN: 接受某个说法、报道或想法是真的
senses.example: I believe his story.
senses.exampleCN: 我相信他的说法。
senses.why: Old English belyfan joined be-, an intensifying prefix, with lyfan, to hold dear or trust, so to believe is to hold a claim as something dear and true.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 belyfan 由起强调作用的 be- 与 lyfan「珍视、信任」组成，所以「相信」就是把某个说法当作珍贵而真实的东西握住。

senses.title: To think or suppose
senses.definition: to think that something is probably the case, often with a softer force than know
senses.definitionCN: 认为某事大概是如此，语气通常比 know 更软
senses.example: I believe she is still at school.
senses.exampleCN: 我想她还在学校。
senses.why: If a claim is held as true without proof, the same verb naturally means to think or suppose, because the speaker is stating an opinion rather than a fact.
senses.whyCN: 如果某个说法在没有证据时也被当作真的握住，这个动词自然就表示「认为、猜想」，因为说话人讲的是看法而不是事实。

senses.title: To hold a religious faith
senses.definition: to have faith in a religion, a god, or a set of teachings
senses.definitionCN: 对某种宗教、神或一套教义怀有信仰
senses.example: Her family believes in God.
senses.exampleCN: 她的家人信仰上帝。
senses.why: The strongest form of holding something true needs no evidence at all, and that is exactly the picture of religious faith, so believe in became the verb of belief.
senses.whyCN: 把某件事当作真实来握住的最强形式完全不需要证据，这正是宗教信仰的画面，于是 believe in 成了表达「信仰」的动词。

senses.title: To trust a person
senses.definition: to have confidence that a person is honest or reliable
senses.definitionCN: 有把握地认为某人诚实可靠
senses.example: I believe in you.
senses.exampleCN: 我信任你。
senses.why: Holding a person dear and trusting their word is the human version of holding a claim true, so the verb also means to trust someone.
senses.whyCN: 珍视一个人并信他的话，是「把说法握为真」在人与人之间的版本，所以这个动词也表示「信任某人」。

senses.title: Hard to accept
senses.definition: used in the negative or in questions to say that something is very surprising
senses.definitionCN: 用于否定句或疑问句，表示某事非常令人惊讶
senses.example: I can't believe you finished so fast.
senses.exampleCN: 我真不敢相信你这么快就做完了。
senses.why: When the mind refuses to hold a claim as true, the negated verb becomes the natural way to express surprise at something hard to accept.
senses.whyCN: 当头脑拒绝把某个说法握为真实时，否定形式的这个动词就成了表达「难以接受、令人吃惊」的自然说法。

intro.en: Believe is an old English compound whose second part meant to hold dear, and the noun belief grew beside it.
intro.cn: believe 是古老的英语复合词，后半意为「珍视」，名词 belief 在它旁边长出来。

items.en: Old English belyfan joined be-, used here for intensity, with lyfan, meaning to hold dear or to trust.
items.cn: 古英语 belyfan 由表强调的 be- 与 lyfan「珍视、信任」组成。

items.en: Lyfan is related to the old adjective lief, meaning dear or pleasing, so trust and affection shared one root.
items.cn: lyfan 与古老形容词 lief「亲爱的、可意的」同源，可见信任与喜爱共用一个词根。

items.en: The verb passed into Middle English with the sense of accepting something as true.
items.cn: 这个动词进入中古英语，意思变成「接受某事为真」。

items.en: The noun belief was formed beside the verb, and the pair has stayed together ever since.
items.cn: 名词 belief 在动词旁边形成，这一对词从此一直并行。

items.en: Believe in became the fixed way to speak of faith in God or in a teaching.
items.cn: believe in 成为表达对上帝或某种教义的信仰的固定说法。

items.en: Today believe covers accepting facts, thinking something likely, holding a faith, and trusting a person.
items.cn: 今天 believe 可指接受事实、认为某事很可能、持有信仰，以及信任一个人。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the noun and adjective family; the near-meaning group collects verbs of thinking, trusting, and doubting.
note.cn: 形近组收名词与形容词词族；近义组收表示「认为、信任、怀疑」的动词。

entries.definition: A person who believes, especially in a religion.

entries.definition: Able to be believed; credible.

entries.definition: Too surprising or strange to be believed.

entries.definition: To have an opinion, matching the suppose sense.

entries.definition: To have confidence in someone's honesty, matching the person sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「信任」，对应「信任某人」义。

entries.definition: To agree that something is true or right, with less feeling than believe.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「接受、认可」，比 believe 少一些情感。

entries.definition: To think something is probably not true; the opposite of the first sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「怀疑」，是第一个义项的反义。

normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的复合成分、真实词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Be- adds force and lyfan means hold dear, so believe is to hold a claim as dear and true.
normal.cn: be- 加强语气，lyfan 表示「珍视」，所以 believe 就是把某个说法当作珍贵而真实的握住。

normal.en: Lyfan is related to lief, meaning dear, so trust and affection grew from one root.
normal.cn: lyfan 与表示「亲爱的」的 lief 同源，可见信任与喜爱出自同一个词根。

normal.en: Belief is the noun, believer the person, believable the adjective.

normal.en: It commonly pairs with in, it or not, and hard to believe.

abstract.en: See one person hand a letter to another and the other nod: that is believe.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人把信递给另一个人，对方点头收下，那就是 believe。

abstract.en: Lay the letter over a church and then over a friend's hand: fact, faith and trust are one gesture.
abstract.cn: 把信叠到教堂上，再叠到朋友手上：事实、信仰与信任是同一个动作。

abstract.en: Say the word, then let the nodding figure bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让点头的身影把意思带回来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「必理吾」——必先讲道理，我才相信你：相信

root: believe 来自古英语 belyfan，由起强调作用的 be- 与 lyfan「珍视、信任」合成，而 lyfan 又与表示「亲爱的」的 lief 同源，所以「相信」原本就是「把某说法当作珍贵而真实的东西握住」。这一动作落在事实上是「相信」，落在猜测上是「认为」，落在宗教上是「信仰」，落在人身上是「信任」。

sensesIntro.en: All five senses of believe come from one gesture: holding something as true and dear, whether a claim, an opinion, a faith, or a person.
sensesIntro.cn: believe 的五个义项都出自同一个动作：把某样东西当作真实又珍贵地握住，无论是说法、看法、信仰，还是一个人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a letter handed over and accepted with a nod
core.cn: 核心意象：一封信被递过去，对方点头收下

branches.en: THE CLAIM: the plainest sense is accepting a statement as true.
branches.cn: 说法线：最朴素的义项就是把一个说法接受为真。

branches.en: THE OPINION: without proof the same hold becomes a softer think or suppose.
branches.cn: 看法线：没有证据时，同一种「握住」变成较软的「认为、猜想」。

branches.en: THE FAITH: the strongest hold needs no evidence and becomes religious belief.
branches.cn: 信仰线：最强的握住不需要证据，于是成为宗教信仰。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the same confidence placed in a human being is trust.
branches.cn: 信任线：把同一种确信放在一个人身上，就是信任。

branches.en: THE REFUSAL: when the mind will not hold the claim, the negative form expresses surprise.
branches.cn: 拒握线：当头脑不肯握住这个说法时，否定形式就用来表达惊讶。

intro.en: Believe is a fused compound; the items below are its old parts, its inflections, and the suffixes that built its family.
intro.cn: believe 是粘合的复合词，下面列出的是它的古老构件、屈折形式和构成词族的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin credere means to trust or believe, and fides means faith; both are parallels to this Germanic verb, not its source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 credere 意为「相信、信任」，fides 意为「信义、信仰」；二者是本词的平行词，而非来源。

items.exampleCN: 它加强 believe 的语气。

items.example: It is the second element of believe.
items.exampleCN: 它是 believe 的第二个成分。

items.example: It forms belief from the same stem.
items.exampleCN: 它在同一词干上构成 belief。

definition_zh: 大脑；头脑、智力；聪明人、主脑；（口语）猛击头部
definition_en: the organ inside the head that controls thought and feeling, the ability to think, or the clever person who plans for a group
core_image: 颅骨里一团掌管思考与记忆的灰白组织
scene: 生物课上，老师指着人体模型说，这团组织让人会思考、会记忆。 The teacher pointed at the model and said the brain controls thought and memory.
sceneCN: 这里 brain 是「大脑」（第 1 个义项：颅腔内主管思维与感觉的器官）；句意为老师指着模型说，大脑控制思维与记忆。

pos.zh: 名词：大脑；头脑；智力；聪明人

derivatives.zh: 由 brain 加 -y 构成，义为「聪明的；有头脑的」
由 brain 加 -less 构成，义为「没头脑的；愚蠢的」
由 brain 与 storm 组合而成，义为「头脑风暴；突然想到的好主意」

senses.title: The organ inside the head
senses.definition: the organ inside the skull that controls thought, memory and feeling
senses.definitionCN: 颅腔内控制思维、记忆与感觉的器官
senses.example: The brain needs oxygen to work well.
senses.exampleCN: 大脑需要氧气才能正常工作。
senses.why: Old English braegen named the soft tissue inside the skull, and this physical sense is still the base of the word.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 braegen 指颅骨内那团柔软的组织，这个实体义至今仍是整个词义的根基。

senses.title: The power to think
senses.definition: the ability to think, learn and understand things
senses.definitionCN: 思考、学习与理解事物的能力
senses.example: It takes brains to solve this puzzle.
senses.exampleCN: 解开这个谜题需要动脑子。
senses.why: Because the organ does the thinking, the word slipped from the flesh to the power that the flesh gives.
senses.whyCN: 因为这团组织负责思考，词义便从肉体本身滑向它带来的思维能力。

senses.title: The clever planner
senses.definition: the most intelligent person in a group, who plans what the others do
senses.definitionCN: 群体中最聪明、为其他人出谋划策的人
senses.example: She is the brains behind the new app.
senses.exampleCN: 她是这款新应用的幕后主脑。
senses.why: A group names its thinker its brain, taking the whole person from the one part that plans the work.
senses.whyCN: 一个群体把出主意的人称作它的 brain，用负责筹划的那一部分来代指整个人。

senses.title: To hit on the head
senses.definition: to hit someone hard on the head, used in informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 口头上指用力击打某人的头部
senses.example: The falling branch brained the careless walker.
senses.exampleCN: 落下的树枝重重砸中了那个不小心的行人。
senses.why: The noun turned into a joke verb: the brain is the target, so hitting the head is to brain someone.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成了带玩笑口气的动词：脑子是受击的部位，所以打头就说成 brain 某人。

intro.en: Brain is an old Germanic word for the tissue inside the skull, and its meaning widened from flesh to thought.
intro.cn: brain 是日耳曼语中表示颅腔内组织的古老词，词义从肉体扩展到思维。

items.en: Braegen named the soft tissue inside the skull and is the oldest recorded form of the word.
items.cn: braegen 指颅骨内的柔软组织，是这个词有记录的最古老形式。

items.en: Dutch and German still have close words for the same organ, which points to one common root.
items.cn: 荷兰语与德语中仍有指同一器官的近亲词，说明它们来自同一个词根。

items.en: The spelling settled as brain, and the word stayed firmly tied to the organ.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 brain，词义仍牢牢系在这个器官上。

items.en: Since the organ does the thinking, the word also came to mean the power to think.
items.cn: 由于这团组织负责思考，这个词又引申为思考的能力。

items.en: Today brain covers the organ, the mind and the clever planner, and it keeps a joking verb.
items.cn: 今天 brain 兼指器官、头脑与聪明的主脑，还保留了一个玩笑式的动词用法。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects words about thinking.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收与思考有关的词。

entries.definition: To make water or liquid flow away.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「排水；流走」，读音与 brain 接近。

entries.definition: The seed of a food plant such as wheat.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「谷物」，拼写与 brain 相近。

entries.definition: A line of railway carriages pulled by an engine.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「火车」，读音与 brain 接近。

entries.definition: The part of a person that thinks and remembers.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「头脑；心智」，指人思考与记忆的部分。

entries.definition: The top part of the body, which holds the brain.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「头」，指身体的顶部。

entries.definition: The ability to learn and understand.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「智力；理解力」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded history, the real family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的历史、真实词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Old English braegen named the tissue inside the skull, and that is still sense one.
normal.cn: 古英语 braegen 指颅骨内的组织，这仍是第一个义项。

normal.en: Because the brain does the thinking, the word grew a second sense: the power to think.
normal.cn: 因为脑子负责思考，这个词长出了第二个义项：思维能力。

normal.en: A group calls its planner its brain, naming the whole person by the part that plans.
normal.cn: 一个群体把出主意的人称作 brain，用筹划的那部分代指整个人。

normal.en: It often pairs with cells, drain and science.
normal.cn: 它常与 cells、drain、science 搭配。

normal.en: Spell b-r-a-i-n; the ai keeps the long vowel.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-r-a-i-n，其中 ai 让元音读长音。

abstract.en: See a pale grey knot inside a glass model of a head: that knot is the brain.
abstract.cn: 想象头部玻璃模型里一团灰白色的组织：那团东西就是 brain。

abstract.en: Let the knot glow and the same picture turns into the power to think.
abstract.cn: 让这团组织亮起来，同一幅画面就变成思考的能力。

abstract.en: Read the word aloud, then let the model bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让那个模型把意思带回来。

examples.en: The brain needs oxygen to work well.
examples.cn: 大脑需要氧气才能正常工作。

examples.en: It takes brains to solve this puzzle.
examples.cn: 解开这个谜题需要动脑子。

examples.en: She is the brains behind the new app.
examples.cn: 她是这款新应用的幕后主脑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「不来音」——颅骨里那团会思考的组织：大脑

root: brain 是日耳曼语中表示颅腔内组织的古老词，古英语写作 braegen，与荷兰语、德语中的近亲词同出一源。因为脑子负责思考，词义从器官扩展到思维能力，又用来称呼群体中出主意的人。今天 brain 兼指大脑、头脑与主脑，还保留了一个表示猛击头部的玩笑式动词用法。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of brain grow from one picture: a grey knot inside the skull that does the thinking.
sensesIntro.cn: brain 的四个义项都从同一个画面生长出来：颅骨里那团负责思考的灰白组织。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grey knot inside the skull that does the thinking
core.cn: 核心意象：颅骨里那团负责思考的灰白组织

branches.en: THE ORGAN: the flesh inside the skull is the first and literal sense.
branches.cn: 器官线：颅内的那团组织是最字面的第一个义项。

branches.en: THE MIND: what the organ does becomes the power to think.
branches.cn: 心智线：这团组织所做的事变成了思考的能力。

branches.en: THE PLANNER: the person who does the thinking for a group.
branches.cn: 主脑线：替一个群体动脑筋的人。

branches.en: THE BLOW: the joking verb aims at the place that holds the brain.
branches.cn: 击打线：玩笑式的动词瞄准装着脑子的部位。

branches.en: THE BASE: the organ and the thinking both rest on the same piece of flesh.
branches.cn: 根基线：器官义与思维义都立在同一块肉体上。

latinIntro.en: Latin cerebrum is the recorded word for the brain; it is a parallel term, not the source of brain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cerebrum 是有记录的「大脑」，它是平行词，不是 brain 的来源。

organized knowledge of the natural world

definition_zh: 秘书；书记；部长
definition_en: a person who handles letters and records for an organization, an official of a club, or a government minister
core_image: 办公桌一角摞着待签的文件，电话听筒还夹在肩头
scene: 她把会议记录整理好，放到经理桌上。 The secretary typed the minutes of the meeting.
sceneCN: 这里 secretary 是「秘书」（第 1 个义项）；句意：秘书打出了会议记录。

senses.title: An office assistant
senses.definition: a person employed to handle letters, records, and office tasks
senses.definitionCN: 受雇处理信件、记录与办公事务的人
senses.example: The secretary answered the phone.
senses.exampleCN: 秘书接了电话。
senses.why: This is the most common modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最常见的现代义。

senses.title: An organization officer
senses.definition: an official who keeps records for a club or organization
senses.definitionCN: 为俱乐部或组织保存记录的负责人
senses.example: She was elected secretary of the club.
senses.exampleCN: 她被选为俱乐部书记。
senses.why: Clubs use the title for their record keeper.
senses.whyCN: 俱乐部用该头衔称呼记录负责人。

senses.title: A government minister
senses.definition: a senior government official in charge of a department
senses.definitionCN: 负责某个部门的高级政府官员
senses.example: The Foreign Secretary gave a speech.
senses.exampleCN: 外交大臣发表了讲话。
senses.why: In some governments the title names a minister.
senses.whyCN: 在某些政府中该头衔指部长。

intro.en: Secretary comes from Latin secretarius, an officer trusted with secrets.
intro.cn: secretary 源自拉丁语 secretarius，指受托掌管机密的人员。

items.en: Secretum meant a secret.
items.cn: secretum 意为秘密。

items.en: Secretarius meant a confidential officer.
items.cn: secretarius 意为掌管机密的人员。

items.en: Secretary entered English for a trusted clerk.
items.cn: secretary 以「受信任的文书」之义进入英语。

items.en: The word spread to clubs and government offices.
items.cn: 该词扩展到俱乐部与政府机构。

items.en: Some countries use it as the title of a minister.

note.en: Secretary is compared with similar-looking words and with words for assistants and officials.

definition_zh: 想知道；纳闷；感到惊讶；惊奇；奇迹；奇观
definition_en: to want to know something, or to feel surprise and admiration; also the feeling or the thing that causes it
core_image: 夜里抬头看见满天星，脖子一直往后仰，忘了低头
scene: 孩子第一次被带到郊外，抬头看星星看了很久，一句话也不说。 I wonder whether the old shop is still open after all these years.
sceneCN: 这里 wonder 是「想知道」（第 1 个义项：心里存着疑问，很想知道答案）；句意为我想知道这么多年过去那家老店是否还开着。夜里仰头看满天星，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 奇迹；奇观；令人惊叹的事物

derivatives.zh: 由 wonder 加 -ful 构成，义为「极好的；精彩的」
由 wonder 加 -ing 构成，义为「好奇的；疑惑的」
由 wonder 加 -ous 构成，义为「奇妙的；令人惊叹的」
由 wonder 加 -ment 构成，义为「惊奇；惊讶之情」

senses.title: To want to know
senses.definition: to feel a wish to know something, often said softly before a polite question
senses.definitionCN: 心里很想弄明白某事，常用在礼貌的提问之前
senses.example: I wonder whether the old shop is still open after all these years.
senses.exampleCN: 我想知道这么多年过去那家老店是否还开着。
senses.why: The old root means to gaze in astonishment, and a mind that keeps gazing turns into a mind that keeps asking.
senses.whyCN: 古老的词根意思是惊讶地凝视，一直望下去的心就变成了不断发问的心。

senses.title: To be struck by something
senses.definition: to feel surprise mixed with admiration when something is greater than expected
senses.definitionCN: 遇到超出预期的事物时，感到惊讶又钦佩
senses.example: The children wondered at the size of the whale in the museum hall.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们望着大厅里那头鲸的骨架，惊讶得说不出话。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer: the body stops and stares because the sight is too large to take in.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层：身体停下凝视，因为眼前的景象大得接不住。

senses.title: The feeling itself
senses.definition: the feeling of surprise and admiration that such a sight leaves behind
senses.definitionCN: 那样的景象留下的那份惊讶与钦佩
senses.example: She looked at the night sky with wonder, forgetting the cold.
senses.exampleCN: 她满怀惊奇地望着夜空，忘了冷。
senses.why: Once the staring ends, what remains inside is the feeling, so the name turns into a noun.
senses.whyCN: 凝视结束之后，留在心里的是那种感受，于是这个名字变成了名词。

senses.title: The thing that causes it
senses.definition: a person or thing so extraordinary that it makes people stare and admire
senses.definitionCN: 极其非凡、让人驻足赞叹的人或物
senses.example: The bridge was counted among the wonders of the ancient world.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥被列为古代世界的奇观之一。
senses.why: By a natural shift, the cause of the staring takes the same name as the staring itself.
senses.whyCN: 很自然的一次转移，让引起凝视的东西和凝视本身用了同一个名字。

intro.en: Wonder comes from Old English wundor, a noun for a marvel, related to words for astonishment in the other Germanic languages.
intro.cn: wonder 来自古英语名词 wundor（奇事），与其他日耳曼语中表示惊讶的词同源。

items.en: wundor named a marvel or a portent, something that stopped people in their tracks.
items.cn: wundor 指奇事或征兆，是让人停下脚步的东西。

items.en: Cousin words in the old Germanic languages also mean a marvel, which points to one shared root.
items.cn: 各门古老日耳曼语里的同源词也表示奇事，指向一个共同词根。

items.en: The noun softened to wonder and gained the sense of a feeling as well as a thing.
items.cn: 名词演变为 wonder，既指事物，也开始指一种感受。

items.en: The verb to wonder developed, first meaning to marvel at, then to be curious.
items.cn: 动词兴起来，先表示对某事惊叹，后来表示好奇。

items.en: The polite opener of requests, as in wonder if, became fixed in everyday speech.
items.cn: 作为礼貌开场的 wonder if，在日常口语中固定下来。

note.en: The first group holds the same stem in other shapes, the second holds other words for curiosity and surprise.
note.cn: 第一组收同一词干的其他形态，第二组收其他表示好奇与惊讶的词。

entries.definition: Extremely good or enjoyable.
entries.definitionCN: 极好的；精彩的

entries.definition: Feeling curious or puzzled.
entries.definitionCN: 好奇的；疑惑的

entries.definition: Marvellous, amazing, a little literary.
entries.definitionCN: 奇妙的；惊人的

entries.definition: To be filled with wonder, or a wonderful thing.
entries.definitionCN: 惊叹；奇迹

entries.definition: A strong wish to know or learn something.
entries.definitionCN: 好奇心

entries.definition: A feeling of respect mixed with wonder and fear.
entries.definitionCN: 敬畏

normalIntro.en: Wonder is one stem used as verb and noun: the same word means to stare, to ask, and the thing worth staring at.
normalIntro.cn: wonder 是同一个词干兼作动词和名词：既指凝视，也指发问，还指值得凝视的东西。

normal.en: The noun and the verb share one spelling, so context alone tells you which is meant.
normal.cn: 名词和动词拼写相同，只能靠上下文判断。

normal.en: No wonder is a frozen phrase that still carries the old idea of marvel.
normal.cn: no wonder 是固定说法，仍带着「奇事」的旧意。

normal.en: Add -ful and the marvel becomes an adjective of praise: wonderful.
normal.cn: 加 -ful，奇事就变成赞美的形容词 wonderful。

normal.en: Wonder if is the soft way to ask a question, not a claim of not knowing.
normal.cn: wonder if 是婉转发问的方式，不是在声称不知道。

normal.en: Wonder and wander differ by one letter: one stays still and stares, the other walks away.
normal.cn: wonder 与 wander 只差一个字母：一个驻足凝视，一个走开。

abstract.en: A neck tipped back so far that the sky fills the whole face.
abstract.cn: 脖子仰得太久，整张脸都是天空。

abstract.en: A question that has no sharp edges yet.
abstract.cn: 一个还没有长出尖角的问题。

abstract.en: A hand lifted but not yet touching the stone of the old bridge.
abstract.cn: 手举起来了，却还没碰到老桥的石头。

examples.en: I wonder why she left without saying goodbye.
examples.cn: 我想知道她为什么不告而别。

examples.en: The children stared at the sea in wonder.
examples.cn: 孩子们惊奇地望着大海。

examples.en: It is no wonder that he passed the exam after months of study.
examples.cn: 他苦读了几个月，通过考试一点也不奇怪。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「望的」——一直往前望着的那个东西，就是让人惊奇的「奇迹」。

root: 古英语名词 wundor（奇事、奇迹），与日耳曼语同源词共同指向「惊奇地凝视」这一核心意象；后派生动词义。

sensesIntro.en: From a stopped body the meaning spreads: first to be struck, then to be curious, then to the feeling, and finally to the thing worth staring at.
sensesIntro.cn: 意义从一个停住的身体散开：先是感到震撼，再是好奇，接着是那份感受，最后是值得凝视的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a neck tipped back until the sky fills the face.
core.cn: 核心意象：仰头到整张脸都是天空。

branches.en: The asking branch: a soft question about the old shop.
branches.cn: 发问分支：轻声问起那家老店。

branches.en: The staring branch: children lost before a whale skeleton.
branches.cn: 凝视分支：孩子在鲸骨架前出神。

branches.en: The feeling branch: wonder under the night sky.
branches.cn: 感受分支：夜空下的惊奇。

branches.en: The marvel branch: a bridge counted among ancient wonders.
branches.cn: 奇观分支：跻身古代奇迹的桥。

branches.en: The everyday branch: no wonder marks surprise that has become ordinary.
branches.cn: 日常分支：no wonder 标记已经平常的惊讶。

intro.en: Wonder is a plain Germanic stem; the endings it takes, such as -ful and -ous, only colour the marvel into adjectives.
intro.cn: wonder 是朴素的日耳曼语词干；它加上的 -ful、-ous 等词尾，只把这件奇事染成形容词。

latinIntro.en: The stem is native Germanic, so there is no Latin ancestor; the Latin words below are cousins of the same idea only.
latinIntro.cn: 词干是本土日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁词只是同一想法的表亲。

items.meaning: a marvel, or to stare and ask
items.example: The stem carries both noun and verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干兼作名词与动词。

items.example: The old marvel sense survives here.
items.exampleCN: 古老的奇事义在此保留。

items.example: The participle shows the stopped body.
items.exampleCN: 分词部分呈现停住的身体。

definition_zh: 金发（的）；浅色的；金发女子
definition_en: having light yellow hair, or a person, especially a woman, with such hair
core_image: 阳光下的一头浅金色长发
scene: 照片里的姑娘站在海边，风吹起她浅金色的长发。 The blonde girl stood by the sea with her hair in the wind.
sceneCN: 这里 blonde 是「金发的」（第 1 个义项：头发呈浅黄色的）；句意为那个金发女孩站在海边，头发随风飘起。

pos.zh: 名词：金发女子；金发的人

derivatives.zh: 同一词的阳性或中性形式，义为「金发的」，美式英语中通用
由 blond 加 -ness 构成，义为「金发；浅色」
由 blond 加 -ish 构成，义为「略带金黄色的」

senses.title: Light yellow hair
senses.definition: having hair of a light yellow or pale golden colour
senses.definitionCN: 头发呈浅黄色或淡金色的
senses.example: She has long blonde hair.
senses.exampleCN: 她留着金色长发。
senses.why: The word came from French blond, and the -e ending still marks the feminine form in careful British use.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自法语 blond，结尾的 -e 在讲究的英式用法里仍标记阴性形式。

senses.title: A person with such hair
senses.definition: a person, especially a woman, with light yellow hair
senses.definitionCN: 头发呈浅黄色的人，尤指女性
senses.example: The blonde walked into the room.
senses.exampleCN: 那位金发女子走进了房间。
senses.why: English often turns an adjective into a noun, so the hair colour can stand for the person who has it.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把形容词直接当名词用，于是发色可以代指拥有这种发色的人。

senses.title: A pale shade
senses.definition: used of wood, beer or other things that have a pale golden colour
senses.definitionCN: 用于木材、啤酒等呈淡金色的东西
senses.example: They ordered two glasses of blonde beer.
senses.exampleCN: 他们点了两杯浅色啤酒。
senses.why: The same pale golden colour appears in wood and beer, so the word stretched from hair to those materials.
senses.whyCN: 同样的淡金色也出现在木材和啤酒里，于是这个词从头发扩展到那些材料。

intro.en: Blonde came into English from French, and its spelling still carries a trace of French gender.
intro.cn: blonde 从法语进入英语，它的拼写仍带着法语性范畴的痕迹。

items.en: Old French blond meant light yellow, and it was used of hair and of pale gold.
items.cn: 古法语 blond 表示浅黄色，用于头发和淡金色。

items.en: The French word probably came from a medieval Latin form used for fair hair.
items.cn: 这个法语词可能来自中世纪拉丁语中描述浅色头发的形式。

items.en: English borrowed blonde in the seventeenth century, mostly to describe women's hair.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 blonde，主要用于描述女性的头发。

items.en: French marks feminine adjectives with -e, and English kept blonde for women and blond for men.
items.cn: 法语用 -e 标记阴性形容词，英语就把 blonde 留给女性，把 blond 留给男性。

items.en: American English now often uses blond for everyone, while British English still prefers blonde for women.
items.cn: 今天美式英语常用 blond 指所有人，英式英语仍偏好用 blonde 指女性。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words close in shape; the near-meaning group collects other hair and colour words.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写接近的词；近义组收其他与头发和颜色有关的词。

entries.definition: The same word without the -e, used for men or for both sexes.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词去掉 -e 的形式，用于男性或不分性别。

entries.definition: A flower, or the state of flowering.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「花；开花」，拼写与 blonde 相近。

entries.definition: Plain, dull and without much taste or interest.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「平淡的；乏味的」，拼写与 blonde 相近。

entries.definition: Light in colour, used of hair or skin.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「浅色的」，可用于头发或皮肤。

entries.definition: Having the colour of gold.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「金色的」。

entries.definition: A woman with dark brown hair, the opposite of a blonde.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「深褐色头发的女子」，与金发女子相对。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded history, the real family, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的历史、真实词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Old French blond meant light yellow and was used of hair and pale gold.
normal.cn: 古法语 blond 表示浅黄色，用于头发和淡金色。

normal.en: English borrowed the word in the seventeenth century, mostly for women's hair.
normal.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个词，主要用于女性的头发。

normal.en: The -e is a French feminine ending, so blonde often points to a woman.
normal.cn: 结尾的 -e 是法语阴性词尾，所以 blonde 常指向女性。

normal.en: It commonly pairs with hair, highlights, woman and beer.
normal.cn: 它常与 hair、highlights、woman、beer 搭配。

normal.en: Spell b-l-o-n-d-e; the silent e marks the feminine form.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-l-o-n-d-e，不发音的 e 标记阴性形式。

abstract.en: See sunlight on pale golden hair by the sea: that colour is blonde.
abstract.cn: 想象海边阳光下浅金色的头发：那种颜色就是 blonde。

abstract.en: Move the same light onto a glass of beer and the word still fits.
abstract.cn: 把同一束光移到一杯啤酒上，这个词仍然适用。

abstract.en: Say the word and let the pale gold bring the sense back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让那抹淡金色把意思带回来。

examples.en: She has long blonde hair.
examples.cn: 她留着金色长发。

examples.en: The blonde walked into the room.
examples.cn: 那位金发女子走进了房间。

examples.en: They ordered two glasses of blonde beer.
examples.cn: 他们点了两杯浅色啤酒。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「布隆德」——阳光照着一头浅金色长发：金发的

root: blonde 来自古法语 blond，表示浅黄色，用于头发与淡金色，可能源自中世纪拉丁语中描述浅色头发的形式。英语在十七世纪借入这个词，主要描述女性头发。法语用 -e 标记阴性，英语因此把 blonde 多用于女性、把 blond 多用于男性；今天美式英语常用 blond 指所有人。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses of blonde come from one picture: a pale golden light, first on hair and then on other materials.
sensesIntro.cn: blonde 的三个义项都来自同一个画面：一抹淡金色的光，先落在头发上，再落到别的材料上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sunlight on pale golden hair
core.cn: 核心意象：阳光照在浅金色的头发上

branches.en: THE HAIR: pale golden hair is the central sense the word was borrowed for.
branches.cn: 头发线：浅金色的头发是这个词被借入时的核心义项。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the adjective becomes a noun for the woman who has such hair.
branches.cn: 人物线：形容词变成名词，指拥有这种发色的女性。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL: wood and beer share the same pale golden shade.
branches.cn: 材料线：木材与啤酒共享同一种淡金色调。

branches.en: THE LOOK: hair colour and the person are one and the same image.
branches.cn: 外观线：发色与拥有发色的人是同一幅画面。

branches.en: THE SHADE: hair and materials are linked by one pale gold colour.
branches.cn: 色调线：头发与材料由同一种淡金色连在一起。

intro.en: Blonde is a borrowed adjective, so the items below are its endings and the words it commonly joins.
intro.cn: blonde 是借入的形容词，下面列出的是它的词尾以及常与它组合的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin flavus and aureus are recorded colour words; they are parallels, not the source of blonde.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 flavus 与 aureus 是有记录的颜色词，它们是平行词，不是 blonde 的来源。

items.example: Blond is the recorded French source.
items.exampleCN: blond 是有记录的法语来源。

items.example: It marks blonde as the feminine spelling.
items.exampleCN: 它标记 blonde 是阴性拼写。

definition_zh: 原谅；饶恕；赦免；（礼貌用语）请再说一遍
definition_en: to forgive someone or officially free them from punishment; a polite word asking someone to repeat
core_image: 松开惩罚的手：本要落下的责罚被收了回去
scene: 听到同桌小声嘀咕了一句没听清，他放下了手中的笔。" Pardon? Could you say that again?" he asked politely.
sceneCN: 这里 pardon 是「（礼貌地）请再说一遍」（第 4 个义项）；句意是他没听清，礼貌地请对方重复一遍。

derivatives.zh: 由 pardon 加形容词后缀 -able 构成，义为「可原谅的」
由否定前缀 un- 加 pardonable 构成，义为「不可原谅的」
由 pardon 加名词后缀 -er 构成，义为「给予原谅（赦免）的人」

senses.title: To forgive an offence
senses.definition: to forgive someone for a fault or wrong they have done
senses.definitionCN: 原谅某人所犯的过失或错误
senses.example: He begged her pardon for arriving so late.
senses.exampleCN: 他为自己迟到这么久请求她的原谅。
senses.why: The core image is withdrawing the hand of punishment; forgiving means pulling back the penalty.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是收回惩罚之手；原谅就是把将要落下的责罚收回去。

senses.title: To officially free from legal punishment
senses.definition: to officially allow someone who has been convicted of a crime to go free or be released from punishment
senses.definitionCN: 官方正式免除被定罪者的刑罚或准予其免受处罚
senses.example: The governor granted a full pardon to the wrongly convicted man.
senses.exampleCN: 州长对蒙冤定罪的男子颁布了完全赦免。
senses.why: The legal sense keeps the same image: the state withdraws a punishment already decided.
senses.whyCN: 法律义项保留同一画面：国家收回已经判定的惩罚。

senses.title: A polite way to say sorry
senses.titleCN: 抱歉；（引起注意或致歉的礼貌语）
senses.definition: a polite expression used to say sorry or to get someone's attention
senses.definitionCN: 表示歉意或引起对方注意的礼貌用语
senses.example: "Pardon me," he said, as he squeezed past the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 「借过一下，」他说着挤过人群。
senses.why: Asking pardon literally means asking to be forgiven for a small disturbance.
senses.whyCN: 说 pardon me 字面上就是请求对方原谅自己小小的打扰。

senses.title: A polite request to repeat
senses.definition: a polite question asking someone to repeat what they said, often because you did not hear it
senses.definitionCN: 礼貌地请对方重复刚才的话，常因没听清
senses.example: "Pardon? I didn't catch your name," she said.
senses.exampleCN: 「您再说一遍好吗？我没听清您的名字，」她说。
senses.why: In British English, rising pardon politely asks the speaker to try again.
senses.whyCN: 在英式英语中，语调上扬的 pardon 礼貌地请对方再说一次。

intro.en: Pardon travelled from Latin through Old French into English, always built on the idea of giving completely and fairly.
intro.cn: pardon 经拉丁语与古法语进入英语，词义始终建立在「完全而公正地给予」这一根义之上。

items.en: The root is perdonare: per- (completely, thoroughly) plus donare (to give), literally "to give wholeheartedly".
items.cn: 词根是拉丁语 perdonare：per-（完全地）加 donare（给予），字面义为「全心全意地给予」。

items.en: Old French pardonner meant to grant, to forgive, and to remit a punishment.
items.cn: 古法语 pardonner 意为给予、宽恕、免除惩罚。

items.en: In medieval church use, perdonare and related forms covered the remission of sins and penalties.
items.cn: 在中世纪教会语境中，perdonare 及相关形式用于表示赦罪与减免惩罚。

items.en: Modern French keeps pardon as both the forgiveness noun and the everyday "sorry" expression.
items.cn: 现代法语中 pardon 既是「宽恕」名词，也是日常表示「抱歉」的用语。

items.en: English took the word from Old French in the 13th century, first in the legal and religious senses.
items.cn: 英语于十三世纪从古法语借入该词，最早用于法律与宗教语境。

items.en: Later uses extended it to polite apologies and the request to repeat a sentence.
items.cn: 后来的用法把它扩展为礼貌致歉语和请对方重复的用语。

note.en: Pardon shares a family with forgive and excuse; the words below are its close neighbours.
note.cn: pardon 与 forgive、excuse 同属一个词族；下列词是它的近邻。

entries.definition: able to be forgiven
entries.definitionCN: 可原谅的；pardon 的形容词派生词

entries.definition: too serious to be forgiven
entries.definitionCN: 不可原谅的；加否定前缀 un- 的派生词

entries.definition: a person who grants pardons or forgiveness
entries.definitionCN: 赦免者；宽恕者；pardon 的名词派生词

entries.definition: made hard or unfeeling; only the ending resembles pardon
entries.definitionCN: 变硬的；冷酷的；词尾拼写相近但词源完全不同

entries.definition: to stop being angry about a fault; general everyday forgiving
entries.definitionCN: 原谅；泛指日常的不计前嫌，语气比 pardon 更温厚

entries.definition: to overlook a small fault or politely allow something
entries.definitionCN: 宽恕；原谅小的过失，也用于礼貌套语 excuse me

entries.definition: to declare in court that someone is not guilty
entries.definitionCN: 宣判无罪；pardon 是事后赦免，acquit 是判决定罪前的开释

entries.definition: an official act of forgiving a group of offenders together
entries.definitionCN: 大赦； amnesty 面向群体，pardon 通常面向个人

normalIntro.en: Break the word into its Latin parts and reuse it in polite phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 把词拆成拉丁成分，并在礼貌用语中反复使用。

normal.en: par- (completely) + don (give): to give completely is to forgive completely.
normal.cn: par-（完全地）加 don（给予）：完全地给予，就是彻底地原谅。

normal.en: don is the give root, the same one as in donate.
normal.cn: don 是「给予」词根，与 donate（捐赠）中的 don 相同。

normal.en: I beg your pardon = I beg your giving-back of the punishment.
normal.cn: I beg your pardon 字面是「恳求您收回责罚」。

normal.en: Pardon my French: pardon me for the rude words.
normal.cn: Pardon my French：为我刚才的粗话求个原谅。

normal.en: In French, pardon itself means sorry — the polite use came straight across.
normal.cn: 法语里 pardon 本身就是「抱歉」，礼貌用法直接从法语移植。

abstract.en: Picture a judge's raised hand slowly lowering: the punishment never falls.
abstract.cn: 想象法官举起的手缓缓放下：惩罚始终没有落下。

abstract.en: A governor signs one paper and a prisoner walks free.
abstract.cn: 州长签下一纸赦令，囚徒从此自由。

abstract.en: You cup your ear: "Pardon?" — asking the sound to come again.
abstract.cn: 你拢起耳朵说「请再说一遍」，恳请那句话重来一次。

examples.en: She pardoned his rudeness, knowing he had been under stress.
examples.cn: 她原谅了他的无礼，知道他一直压力很大。

examples.en: The president granted a pardon to the former prisoner.
examples.cn: 总统对这名前囚徒颁布了赦免。

examples.en: "Pardon?" he asked, leaning closer to hear the announcement.
examples.cn: 「您能再说一遍吗？」他凑近去听广播。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕等」——pardon 谐音「怕等」：求人原谅的人最「怕等」，怕对方不肯收回责罚；听到没听清也「怕等」不了，赶紧说句 pardon 请对方再说一遍。

root: pardon 源自拉丁语 perdonare，由 per-（完全地）与 donare（给予）构成，字面义为「全心全意地给予」；经古法语 pardonner 于十三世纪进入英语，词义由「宽恕」扩展到「赦免」与礼貌套语。

sensesIntro.en: From forgiving a personal wrong, pardon widens to official remission of punishment, then narrows into polite formulas for apology and for asking a speaker to repeat.
sensesIntro.cn: 从原谅个人过错出发，pardon 扩展到官方赦免刑罚，再收窄为致歉与请人复述的礼貌用语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: withdrawing the hand of punishment
core.cn: 核心意象：收回即将落下的惩罚之手

branches.en: Forgiving a personal fault
branches.cn: 原谅个人的过失

branches.en: Officially releasing someone from legal punishment
branches.cn: 正式赦免刑罚

branches.en: Polite apology for a small disturbance
branches.cn: 为小打扰致歉

branches.en: Politely asking for a sentence to be repeated
branches.cn: 礼貌请求复述

branches.en: Everyday formulas built on asking forgiveness
branches.cn: 建立在求恕之上的日常套语

intro.en: The per- plus don- skeleton explains both the meaning and the family of pardon words.
intro.cn: per- 加 don- 的骨架既解释了词义，也串起了 pardon 词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root donare, to give, also produced donate, donor, and donation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 donare（给予）还派生出 donate、donor、donation 等词。

definition_zh: 已经；早已；先前
definition_en: before now, or sooner than was expected
core_image: 桌上的饭菜已经摆好等人来
scene: 客人还没到，桌上的饭菜已经摆好了。 The meal was already ready.
sceneCN: 这里 already 是「已经」（第 1 个义项：在现在之前完成）；句意为饭菜已经准备好了。

senses.title: Before now
senses.definition: at a time earlier than the present
senses.definitionCN: 比现在更早的时间
senses.example: I have already read the book.
senses.exampleCN: 我已经读过这本书了。
senses.why: All ready meant fully prepared, and work that is prepared is done before the present.
senses.whyCN: all ready 意为完全准备好，准备好的事自然在现在之前完成。

senses.title: Sooner than expected
senses.definition: earlier than someone thought it would be
senses.definitionCN: 比别人以为的更早
senses.example: Are you leaving already?
senses.exampleCN: 你就要走了吗？
senses.why: A finished state seen too early in the day gives the surprised sense of sooner than expected.
senses.whyCN: 在一天里过早看到「已完成」的状态，就产生「比预期更早」的惊讶。

definition_zh: 回答；答案；应门；满足
definition_en: words given in reply, or the solution to a problem, or a reply to a call
core_image: 老师提问，学生举手回答
scene: 课堂上，老师刚提问，一名学生就举起手回答。 She answered the question at once.
sceneCN: 这里 answered 是「回答」（第 1 个义项：口头答复）；句意为她立刻回答了问题。

senses.title: Words in reply
senses.definition: words spoken or written back to a question
senses.definitionCN: 针对提问说回或写回的话
senses.example: She answered the question at once.
senses.exampleCN: 她立刻回答了问题。
senses.why: The old word meant a sworn reply, so words returned to a question are the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 古词意为宣誓后的答复，所以对问题说回去的话是第一义。

senses.title: The correct solution
senses.definition: the correct reply to a problem or a test
senses.definitionCN: 对题目或试题的正确解答
senses.example: The answer to the puzzle is three.
senses.exampleCN: 这道谜题的答案是三。
senses.why: A reply is right or wrong, and the right one becomes the solution called an answer.
senses.whyCN: 答复有对有错，正确的那一个就成了所谓答案。

senses.title: To reply to a call
senses.definition: to open the door or pick up the phone when someone calls
senses.definitionCN: 有人叫门或来电时去开门或接听
senses.example: Nobody answered the door.
senses.exampleCN: 没有人去应门。
senses.why: A knock or a ring is also a question, and going to it is answering in action.
senses.whyCN: 敲门或铃声也是一种提问，去回应就是行动上的回答。

senses.title: To be enough for a need
senses.definition: to be enough for what is needed
senses.definitionCN: 足以应付需要
senses.example: This small room answers our need.
senses.exampleCN: 这间小房间满足了我们的需要。
senses.why: When a thing replies to a demand by being enough, the reply sense turns into satisfying.
senses.whyCN: 当某物以「足够」来回应需求，回答之义就转成满足。
