definition_zh: 小路；小径；路线；路径；途径；道路
definition_en: a narrow way made for walking, the route along which someone or something travels, a course of action in life, or the chain of folders that locates a file
core_image: 湿叶覆盖的一条窄土路，尽头是湖
scene: 雨后的林子里，落叶铺满一条窄窄的土路，尽头通向湖边。 We followed the path down to the lake.
sceneCN: 这里的 path 是「小路、小径」（第 1 个义项：供人行走的窄道）；句意是我们沿着这条小路走到湖边。图中可辨识物件：落叶、窄土路、湖面。

pos.zh: 小路；小径；路线；路径；途径

derivatives.zh: 由 path 与 way 复合而成，义为「通道；路径」
由 path 加否定后缀 -less 构成，义为「无路的」
由 path 与 finder 复合而成，义为「探路者；开创者」

senses.title: A narrow track for walking
senses.definition: a narrow way made for walking, especially across fields or through woods
senses.definitionCN: 供人行走的窄道，尤指穿过田野或树林的
senses.example: We followed the path down to the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 我们沿着这条小路走到湖边。
senses.why: Path in Old English named ground worn by feet, so the first sense is physical: a line that people make simply by walking it.
senses.whyCN: 古英语的 path 指被脚踩出来的地面，所以第一个义项是实体的：一条人走着走着就形成的线。

senses.title: The route from one place to another
senses.definition: the line along which someone or something moves or travels from one point to another
senses.definitionCN: 人或物从一地移动到另一地所经过的线
senses.example: The storm changed the path of the flight.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴改变了航班的航线。
senses.why: Once a track is seen from above as a line, it can belong to anything that moves, whether feet, a plane or a beam of light.
senses.whyCN: 一条小径从高处看就是一条线，于是它可以属于任何会移动的东西：脚步、飞机或一束光。

senses.title: A course of action in life
senses.definition: a way of living or acting that leads towards a particular result
senses.definitionCN: 通向某种结果的生活方式或行动方向
senses.example: She chose a path that her parents had never taken.
senses.exampleCN: 她选了一条父母从未走过的路。
senses.why: A route leads to a destination, and a career also has a direction, so the walking word is borrowed whenever a choice has a destination in view.
senses.whyCN: 路线通向目的地，人生也有方向，所以只要一个选择看得见终点，这个走路的词就会被借去使用。

senses.title: A location in a computer system
senses.definition: the set of folders that shows where a file is stored, or the route data takes through a network
senses.definitionCN: 标明文件存放位置的文件夹序列，或数据在网络中经过的路线
senses.example: Copy the file path into the search box.
senses.exampleCN: 把文件路径复制到搜索框里。
senses.why: A file sits at the end of a chain of folders, and that chain is read as a route, so the old walking word serves computing without changing shape.
senses.whyCN: 一个文件位于一串文件夹的末端，而这一串被读成一条路线，于是这个古老的走路词原样服务于计算机。

intro.en: Path goes back to Old English pæþ and to a West Germanic word for a track, reconstructed as patha; its deeper origin is uncertain, and it has no reliable Latin relative.
intro.cn: path 上溯古英语 pæþ，再上溯到一个表示「小径」的西日耳曼语词，重构形式为 patha；更早的来源不确定，也没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

items.en: A word reconstructed as patha named a track or a worn way, and it is the common ancestor of English path and German Pfad.
items.cn: 一个重构为 patha 的词表示小径或踩出来的路，它是英语 path 与德语 Pfad 的共同祖先。

items.en: Old English wrote the word pæþ and used it for a narrow way on the ground, with the th written by a runic letter.
items.cn: 古英语把这个词写作 pæþ，用来指地面上的一条窄路，其中的 th 音用一枚卢恩字母书写。

items.en: Middle English path kept the physical track and began to be used for the course of a journey or of a life.
items.cn: 中古英语的 path 保留实体的路径，并开始用来指一段行程或一生的走向。

items.en: Writers of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries made path to success and path of duty ordinary phrases.
items.cn: 十六、十七世纪的作者让「通往成功之路」与「责任之路」成为寻常说法。

items.en: Modern English adds the computing sense, where a path lists the folders passed through to reach a file.
items.cn: 现代英语添上计算机义：path 列出到达某个文件所经过的各个文件夹。

note.en: The look-alike group shows the compounds built on path and two Greek-derived words that merely share its spelling; the near-meaning group gathers words for tracks and routes.
note.cn: 形近组展示由 path 构成的复合词，以及两个只是拼写相近的希腊语来源词；近义组收表示小径与路线的词。

entries.definition: A narrow path made for people on foot.
entries.definitionCN: 专供步行者走的窄道。

entries.definition: A quality in art or speech that stirs pity or sadness.

entries.definition: Arousing pity, or so poor as to be contemptible.
entries.definitionCN: 引起怜悯的，或差得令人轻视的。

entries.definition: A rough path or the marks left by something moving.
entries.definitionCN: 崎岖的小道，或移动之物留下的痕迹。

entries.definition: A path through wild country, often narrow and unpaved.
entries.definitionCN: 穿过荒野的小径，通常狭窄且未铺砌。

entries.definition: The way taken from a starting point to a destination.
entries.definitionCN: 从起点到终点所走的路。

entries.definition: A road, a direction, or a method of doing something.
entries.definitionCN: 道路、方向，或做某事的方法。

normalIntro.en: Path is a native English word of uncertain deeper origin, and its hooks follow a line on the ground as it becomes a route, a life choice and finally a folder chain.
normalIntro.cn: path 是英语本族词，更早的来源不确定；记忆钩子顺着地面上的一条线，看它变成路线、人生选择，最后变成一串文件夹。

normal.en: Old English pæþ is the same word in older spelling, and the th was once written with a runic letter rather than two letters.
normal.cn: 古英语 pæþ 就是同一个词的旧拼写，其中的 th 一度用卢恩字母而不是两个字母书写。

normal.en: German Pfad and English path descend from one West Germanic word, which is why they look and sound like cousins.
normal.cn: 德语 Pfad 与英语 path 同出一个西日耳曼语词，所以它们看起来、听起来都像表亲。

normal.en: Pathway and footpath add a second noun instead of changing path itself, so the base word stays visible inside them.
normal.cn: pathway 与 footpath 都是再加一个名词，而不是改变 path 本身，所以基础词在它们里面仍然看得见。

normal.en: Pathless uses -less to say that no track exists, which is the same ending as in hopeless and careless.
normal.cn: pathless 用 -less 表示没有路，和 hopeless、careless 用的是同一个词尾。

normal.en: In computing a path is still a route: folders are places, and the path gives the order in which to pass through them.
normal.cn: 在计算机里，path 仍然是路线：文件夹是一个个地点，路径给出依次穿过的顺序。

abstract.en: A path is made by repetition: one walker leaves nothing, but enough feet wear a line into the ground.
abstract.cn: 路是被重复走出来的：一个人走过不留痕迹，脚足够多就把一条线磨进地面。

abstract.en: The word means both the line and the direction, which is why a life can be said to have a path without any ground under it.
abstract.cn: 这个词既指那条线，也指方向，所以人生即使脚下没有土地，也能说有一条 path。

abstract.en: Pathos looks like path but comes from Greek suffering, a reminder that two similar shapes can carry unrelated histories.
abstract.cn: pathos 看起来像 path，却来自希腊语中「受苦」一词，提醒人两个相似的形状可能背负毫不相干的历史。

examples.en: We followed the path down to the lake.
examples.cn: 我们沿着这条小路走到湖边。

examples.en: The storm changed the path of the flight.
examples.cn: 风暴改变了航班的航线。

examples.en: Copy the file path into the search box.
examples.cn: 把文件路径复制到搜索框里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爬石」——山间小路全是石头，得一步步爬过去；记住 path 是小路，也是路径。

root: 古英语 pæþ（小路）与德语 Pfad 同出西日耳曼语重构形式 patha，更早来源不确定；没有可靠的拉丁同族词，希腊语 pathos（受苦）只是拼写相近，与此词无关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a line worn by feet; the senses divide into the narrow track, the route of anything that moves, the course of a life and the folder chain of a file.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是被脚踩出来的一条线；义项按「窄窄的小径」「任何移动之物的路线」「人生的走向」「文件的文件夹链」分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow soil track under wet leaves, leading to a lake.
core.cn: 核心意象：湿叶覆盖的一条窄土路，尽头是湖。

branches.en: wet leaves over a soil track
branches.cn: 湿叶盖住的土路

branches.en: a gap in a hedge made by walkers
branches.cn: 行人踩出的树篱缺口

branches.en: a flight redrawn around a storm
branches.cn: 为避开风暴而改画的航线

branches.en: a choice neither parent had made
branches.cn: 父母都没做过的选择

branches.en: a folder chain ending at one file
branches.cn: 以单个文件结尾的文件夹链

intro.en: Path is a bare Old English noun, so the entries below show the plural ending, the privative suffix and the compounds English built on it.
intro.cn: path 是一个朴素的古英语名词，因此下面列出它的复数词尾、否定后缀，以及英语在其上构成的复合词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for path; the resemblance to Greek pathos is accidental, so no Latin entry is listed.
latinIntro.cn: path 没有可靠的拉丁同族词；它与希腊语 pathos 的相似只是巧合，因此不列拉丁词条。

items.meaningCN: 复数词尾：清音 th 后加 -s

items.meaning: opening a new route or field
the route to a stored file

definition_zh: 行星；地球（作为人类家园时的指称）；（占星）行星（含日月）
definition_en: a large round body that orbits a star and has cleared its own path of smaller debris, or such a body in general speech
core_image: 望远镜目镜里一颗带条纹的圆球悬在黑色背景中，旁边有一条细细的光环
scene: 望远镜前，一颗带条纹的圆球悬在黑色背景里，旁边有一条细细的光环。 A single planet hangs in the eyepiece, striped and ringed.
sceneCN: 这里 planet 指「绕恒星运行、近似球形并清空轨道附近的大天体」（第 1 个义项：天文学的定义）；句意为目镜中悬着一颗有条纹、带环的行星。图中可辨识物件：目镜筒、带条纹圆球、细光环、黑色背景、支架；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 行星；地球；占星意义上的行星（含日月）

collocations.zh: 绕其他恒星运行的行星

senses.title: The IAU definition
senses.titleCN: 天文学定义：绕恒星、近似球形、清空轨道
senses.definition: a body that orbits the sun or another star, is massive enough to be nearly round, and has cleared its neighbourhood of comparable bodies
senses.definitionCN: 绕太阳或其他恒星运行、质量足以近似球形，并已清空轨道附近同类天体的天体
senses.example: A single planet hangs in the eyepiece, striped and ringed.
senses.exampleCN: 目镜中悬着一颗有条纹、带环的行星。
senses.why: the definition was tightened in 2006 to separate planets from the many similar-sized bodies in belts, so three conditions replaced the older informal one.
senses.whyCN: 这一定义在 2006 年被收紧，以把行星与带中大量同样大小的天体区分开，于是三条条件取代了旧的松散说法。

senses.title: One of the eight
senses.definition: one of the eight bodies recognised in the solar system, from Mercury to Neptune
senses.definitionCN: 太阳系中公认的八颗天体之一，从水星到海王星
senses.example: Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system.
senses.exampleCN: 木星是太阳系中最大的行星。
senses.why: everyday use keeps the older, simpler list, so 'planet' usually means one of the eight even in careful speech.
senses.whyCN: 日常用法沿用更旧、更简单的名单，因此即使在谨慎的说法里，planet 通常也指八颗之一。

senses.title: A planet of another star
senses.titleCN: 其他恒星的行星（系外行星）
senses.definition: used with modifiers for bodies orbiting stars other than the sun
senses.definitionCN: 与修饰语连用，指绕太阳以外恒星运行的天体
senses.example: The telescope found a planet in a tight four-day orbit.
senses.exampleCN: 望远镜发现了一颗四天就绕一圈的行星。
senses.why: once other stars were known to have such bodies, the noun needed no new word; the modifier carries the difference.
senses.whyCN: 当其他恒星被确认拥有这类天体后，这个名词无需新词，差别由修饰语承担。

senses.title: Dwarf planet as a boundary case
senses.definition: used in the compound dwarf planet for a round body that has not cleared its neighbourhood, such as Pluto
senses.definitionCN: 用于复合词「矮行星」，指近似球形但未清空轨道附近的天体，如冥王星
senses.example: Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.
senses.exampleCN: 冥王星在 2006 年被改归为矮行星。
senses.why: the boundary had to be drawn somewhere, and the compound keeps the old word while marking the failed third condition.
senses.whyCN: 边界总得画在某处，而这个复合词保留了旧词，同时标出它未满足第三条条件。

senses.title: The earth as 'the planet'
senses.definition: used with the definite article to mean the earth, especially in environmental talk
senses.definitionCN: 带定冠词时指地球，尤用于环境话题
senses.example: We treat the planet as if its resources had no limit.
senses.exampleCN: 我们把这颗行星当作资源没有上限。
senses.why: seen from outside, the earth is simply one planet, so the definite noun becomes a way of speaking about all of us at once.
senses.whyCN: 从外面看，地球只是一颗行星，因此这个带冠词的名词成了一种把所有人一起谈论的说法。

senses.title: Living on another planet
senses.titleCN: 比喻：心不在焉、脱离现实
senses.definition: in the phrase on another planet, describing someone out of touch with present reality
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语「在另一颗行星上」，形容某人心不在焉、脱离现实
senses.example: His plan was elegant and completely on another planet.
senses.exampleCN: 他的方案很精巧，却完全不接地气。
senses.why: the image works because another planet is a place with different rules, so a person out of touch seems to live there.
senses.whyCN: 这个意象成立，是因为另一颗行星是一个规则不同的地方，脱离现实的人仿佛就住在那儿。

senses.title: Astrology's seven planets
senses.titleCN: 占星中的七行星（含日月）
senses.definition: in astrology, one of the seven traditional bodies: sun, moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn
senses.definitionCN: 占星中七颗传统天体之一：日、月、水星、金星、火星、木星与土星
senses.example: Old charts assign each planet a day of the week.
senses.exampleCN: 旧星盘为每颗行星分配一周中的一天。
senses.why: astrology preserves the ancient list in which the sun and moon also wandered, so its 'planets' are not the astronomer's.
senses.whyCN: 占星保留了太阳与月亮也会游走的古老名单，因此它的「行星」并非天文学家的行星。

senses.title: The old wandering stars
senses.definition: historically, any of the lights that moved against the fixed stars, including the sun and moon
senses.definitionCN: 历史上指任何相对于恒星移动的光点，包括太阳与月亮
senses.example: Ancient observers counted seven planets, sun and moon included.
senses.exampleCN: 古代观测者数出七颗行星，日月也在其中。
senses.why: the word meant 'wanderer' before it meant 'world', so the older list follows the original meaning rather than the modern one.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在指「世界」之前意为「漫游者」，因此旧的名单遵循原义而非今义。

senses.title: A world in fiction
senses.titleCN: 虚构作品中的「行星世界」
senses.definition: used in science fiction for a habitable or visited world with its own conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在科幻作品中指可居住或可造访、有自身条件的世界
senses.example: The crew landed on a planet where a day lasts a month.
senses.exampleCN: 船员降落在一颗一天长达一个月的行星上。
senses.why: stories need a unit of setting larger than a country and smaller than a galaxy, and the planet supplies exactly that.
senses.whyCN: 故事需要一个大于国家、小于星系的设定单位，而行星恰好提供了它。

intro.en: Planet comes from Greek planētēs 'wanderer', through Latin planeta and Old French. The word meant a moving star long before it meant a world. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: planet 来自希腊 planētēs「漫游者」，经拉丁 planeta 与古法语进入英语。在它指「世界」之前，很久以来都指会移动的星。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek astronomers called the five moving lights planētēs, 'wanderers', because they drifted against the fixed stars.
items.cn: 希腊天文学家把五个移动的光点称作 planētēs「漫游者」，因为它们相对恒星漂移。

items.en: Latin borrowed the noun as planeta and kept the meaning 'wandering star'; the sun and moon were often counted among them.
items.cn: 拉丁语借作 planeta，保留「游星」之义；太阳与月亮常被算在其中。

items.en: Old French planete carried the word into English in the Middle Ages, still as an astronomical body rather than a world.
items.cn: 古法语 planete 在中世纪把这个词带入英语，仍指天文天体而非一个世界。

items.en: From the seventeenth century telescopes showed planets as disks and worlds, and the word shifted from 'moving light' to 'physical body'.
items.cn: 从 17 世纪起，望远镜让行星显出圆盘与世界的模样，这个词便从「移动的光」转为「实体天体」。

items.en: The International Astronomical Union fixed three conditions in 2006 and created the dwarf planet category for bodies that fail the third.
items.cn: 国际天文学联合会在 2006 年定下三条条件，并为未满足第三条的天体设立「矮行星」类别。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Greek history of planasthai 'to wander' is not established, and any older Indo-European form proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：planasthai「漫游」在希腊语之前的历史没有定论，凡为其提出的更早印欧形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words derived from planet that name related bodies; group two holds sky objects that are often mistaken for planets.
note.cn: 第一组是由 planet 派生、指相关天体的词；第二组是常被误认作行星的天空对象。

entries.definition: The adjective of planet; it describes relations and systems rather than naming a body.
entries.definitionCN: planet 的形容词；描述关系与系统，而非命名天体。

entries.definition: A small body that looks like a planet but is not one; the -oid suffix marks resemblance, not membership.
entries.definitionCN: 形似行星而非行星的小天体；-oid 后缀标记相似而非归类。

entries.definition: One of the small bodies that collide and grow into planets; it is a stage, not a category of planet.
entries.definitionCN: 碰撞并长成行星的小天体之一；它是一个阶段，而非行星的一个类别。

entries.definition: Exo- 'outside' plus planet: a planet of a star other than the sun, so the head noun is still planet.
entries.definitionCN: exo-「在外」加 planet：太阳以外某颗恒星的行星，中心词仍是 planet。

entries.definition: A body that shines by its own fusion; planets only reflect light, which is why the two were once distinguished by motion.
entries.definitionCN: 靠自身核聚变发光的天体；行星只反射光，这正是两词最初靠运动来区分的原因。

entries.definition: A natural body orbiting a planet; a planet orbits a star, so the two words mark different centres.
entries.definitionCN: 绕行星运行的天然天体；行星绕恒星，因此两词标记不同的中心。

entries.definition: A place with its own conditions, often used for planets in fiction; it is a broader, older word.
entries.definitionCN: 有自身条件的地方，常用于虚构中的行星；是更宽、更古老的词。

entries.definition: The neutral word for any discrete object in space, used when the class is unknown or unimportant.
entries.definitionCN: 指太空中任何独立天体的中性词，用于类别未知或不重要时。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real compounds, real relatives and real history, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的搭配、真实同族词与真实历史，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek planētēs 'wanderer': planets were the lights that wandered.
normal.cn: 希腊 planētēs「漫游者」：行星就是会漫游的光点。

normal.en: The family runs planet, planets, planetary, planetoid, planetesimal, exoplanet.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 planet、planets、planetary、planetoid、planetesimal、exoplanet。

normal.en: Three IAU conditions: orbit a star, be nearly round, clear the neighbourhood.
normal.cn: 国际天文学联合会三条条件：绕恒星、近似球形、清空轨道附近。

normal.en: The eight are Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.
normal.cn: 八颗是水星、金星、地球、火星、木星、土星、天王星、海王星。

normal.en: Astrology still counts sun and moon among its seven planets.
normal.cn: 占星仍把太阳与月亮算在它的七颗行星中。

abstract.en: Picture a marble circling a lamp in a dark room.
abstract.cn: 想象暗室里一颗弹珠绕着一盏灯转。

abstract.en: Picture a single room that must hold everyone's weather at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一个房间必须同时装下所有人的天气。

abstract.en: Picture a stranger who follows rules from a place nobody else can see.
abstract.cn: 想象一个按别人看不见的地方的规则行事的陌生人。

examples.en: Mercury is the smallest planet and the closest to the sun.
examples.cn: 水星是最小的行星，也是离太阳最近的一颗。

examples.en: Planets form from the same disk of dust that makes their star.
examples.cn: 行星由构成其恒星的同一片尘埃盘形成。

examples.en: The probe will study the planet's thin atmosphere from orbit.
examples.cn: 探测器将在轨道上研究这颗行星的稀薄大气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普拉内特（planet）」——天上到处乱跑的那颗球 → 行星

root: 希腊 planētēs「漫游者」← planasthai「漫游」，经拉丁 planeta、古法语 planete 进入英语；今义经望远镜观测由「移动的光」转为「实体世界」。planasthai 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses begin with the tightened definition, move to the eight, to other stars' planets and the dwarf boundary, then to the earth itself, a metaphor, astrology, the old list and fiction.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项先从收紧后的定义开始，再到八颗行星、别的恒星的行星与矮行星边界，然后到地球本身、一个比喻、占星、旧名单与虚构作品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one round body held in a path around a much larger light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个圆体被维持在一条绕更大光源的路径上。

branches.en: DEFINITION AND LIST: a strict rule and the familiar eight answer the same question at different depths.
branches.cn: 定义与名单：严格规则与熟悉的八颗在不同深度回答同一个问题。

branches.en: EDGES OF THE CLASS: other stars' planets and dwarf planets test where the word stops.
branches.cn: 类别的边缘：别恒星的行星与矮行星都在试探这个词的边界。

branches.en: ONE PLANET, TWO VIEWS: the earth as home, and a metaphor for being out of touch.
branches.cn: 一颗行星两种看法：作为家园的地球，以及脱离现实的比喻。

branches.en: OLD LISTS: astrology and ancient astronomy keep sun and moon inside the word.
branches.cn: 旧名单：占星与古代天文学把日月留在词内。

branches.en: STAGE OF A STORY: fiction uses the planet as its unit of setting.
branches.cn: 故事的舞台：虚构作品把行星当作设定单位。

intro.en: Planet is a Greek noun borrowed through Latin; English builds a large family from it with suffixes for relation, resemblance and size.
intro.cn: planet 是经拉丁借入的希腊名词；英语用表示关系、相似与大小的后缀从中构建了一个大词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin planeta and the adjective planetarius carry the word; Latin also said stella errans 'wandering star' for the same object.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 planeta 与形容词 planetarius 承载这个词；拉丁也用 stella errans「游星」指同一对象。

items.example: The Greek word named the moving lights.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊词命名了会移动的光点。
拉丁语保留了天文学义。

items.example: The planet has a four-day year.
items.exampleCN: 这颗行星的一年只有四天。

items.example: The eight planets differ greatly in size.
items.exampleCN: 八大行星大小差异极大。

items.example: Planetary science grew from telescope work.
items.exampleCN: 行星科学由望远镜工作发展而来。

items.example: The planetoid orbits between Mars and Jupiter.
items.exampleCN: 这个小行星体在火星与木星之间运行。

items.example: Planetesimals stuck together in the early disk.
items.exampleCN: 早期盘中星子粘合在一起。

items.example: Thousands of exoplanets are now known.
items.exampleCN: 现已知道数千颗系外行星。

stella errans (noun phrase, first declension + present participle)
planetarius, planetaria, planetarium (adj., first and second declension)

definition_zh: 木材；木头；树林；林地；木（球杆；乐器类别）
definition_en: the hard material of trees used for building, or a small forest; also the hard core of a golf club
core_image: 刚锯开的木头横截面，年轮一圈套一圈，还带着潮气
scene: 院子里新锯断的树桩还没搬走，切面上能数出一圈圈的年轮。 The table is made of old oak wood that has turned dark with time.
sceneCN: 这里 wood 是「木材、木头」（第 1 个义项：树木的坚硬材料，用来做东西）；句意为这张桌子是用年久变深的老橡木做的。新锯开的横截面上能数出年轮，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 wood 加 -en 构成，义为「木制的；僵硬的」
由 wood 加 -y 构成，义为「木质化的；树木茂密的」
由 wood 与 land 复合，义为「林地」
由 wood 与 work 复合，义为「木工活；木制部件」

senses.title: The material of a tree
senses.definition: the hard substance inside a tree, cut and used for building or burning
senses.definitionCN: 树干内部的坚硬物质，砍下后用于建造或燃烧
senses.example: The table is made of old oak wood that has turned dark with time.
senses.exampleCN: 这张桌子是用年久变深的老橡木做的。
senses.why: The oldest meaning is the substance itself, the part of the tree that can be carried away and used.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是那种物质本身，也就是树身上能够搬走使用的那部分。

senses.title: A small forest
senses.definition: a piece of land covered with growing trees, smaller than a forest, often in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 一片长着活树的土地，比 forest 小，常用复数
senses.example: We walked through the woods behind the farm until it got dark.
senses.exampleCN: 我们穿过农舍后面的树林，一直走到天黑。
senses.why: Where the material grows in plenty, the same name serves for the place, and the plural marks the many trees.
senses.whyCN: 那种材料长得多的地方也用了同一个名字，复数则点出许多棵树。

senses.title: The hard core of a club
senses.definition: the solid block of a golf club that strikes the ball, once made of wood
senses.definitionCN: 高尔夫球杆击球的那块实心部分，早年用木头制成
senses.example: He hit the ball with the wood instead of the iron on the short hole.
senses.exampleCN: 那洞很短，他用木杆而不是铁杆击球。
senses.why: Because clubs were once carved from hard timber, the material name stuck to the part.
senses.whyCN: 因为球杆早年用硬木削成，材料名就留在了那个部件上。

senses.title: A wooden sound
senses.definition: used to describe a wooden or dull quality, or the section of an orchestra that was once wooden
senses.definitionCN: 用来形容木质的、发闷的特质，也指乐团中过去用木制成的声部
senses.example: The wood section began softly, and the strings came in a beat later.
senses.exampleCN: 木管声部轻轻开始，弦乐晚了一拍进来。
senses.why: Material used as an adjective easily becomes a label for sound or class, not only for substance.
senses.whyCN: 材料名作形容词用，很容易变成声音或类别的标签，而不只是指物质。

intro.en: Wood is Old English wudu, meaning both the tree and its timber, and the same stem survives in the Dutch and German names for wood.
intro.cn: wood 来自古英语 wudu，既指树也指木材，同一词干还见于荷兰语和德语的「木头」。

items.en: wudu named both a growing tree and the timber cut from it.
items.cn: wudu 既指生长着的树，也指砍下的木材。

items.en: Cousin words in Dutch and German still mean wood or forest.
items.cn: 荷兰语与德语的同源词仍表示木头或森林。

items.en: The final vowel weakened, and the form settled toward wode and later wood.
items.cn: 词尾元音弱化，形式向 wode 过渡，最终成为 wood。

items.en: The wooden adjective took the old ending -en, as in golden and silken.
items.cn: 木制的形容词采用了古老的词尾 -en，就像 golden 与 silken。

items.en: The plural woods narrowed mostly to the place sense, the trees standing together.
items.cn: 复数 woods 主要收窄到地方义，即聚在一起的树。

note.en: The first group holds words grown from the same stem, the second holds other words for timber and for small forests.
note.cn: 第一组收同根长出的词，第二组收其他泛指木材与树林的词。

entries.definition: Made of wood; also stiff and unnatural.
entries.definitionCN: 木制的；僵硬的

entries.definition: Having a lot of wood in it, or full of trees.
entries.definitionCN: 木质化的；树木茂密的

entries.definition: Land covered with trees.
entries.definitionCN: 林地

entries.definition: Wood prepared for building, often large beams.
entries.definitionCN: 木材；木料

entries.definition: Timber cut into rough boards, chiefly American.
entries.definitionCN: 木料（多用于美式）

entries.definition: A large area thickly covered with trees.
entries.definitionCN: 森林

normalIntro.en: Wood is one short native word with a double life: growing trees and the timber cut from them.
normalIntro.cn: wood 是一个简短的本土词，过着双重生活：既指活树，也指砍下来的木头。

normal.en: The plural woods usually means a place full of trees, not several materials.
normal.cn: 复数 woods 通常指满是树的地方，而不是好几种木头。

normal.en: Wooden takes the old ending -en, the same one in golden.
normal.cn: wooden 用古老的词尾 -en，与 golden 相同。

normal.en: Woody adds -y and keeps both letters of the stem: wood plus y.
normal.cn: woody 加 -y 时保留词干的两个字母：wood 加 y。

normal.en: Do not confuse wood with would: one is material, the other a helping verb.
normal.cn: 别把 wood 与 would 混了：一个是材料，一个是助动词。

normal.en: Woodland and woodwork are compounds that join a second common word.
normal.cn: woodland 与 woodwork 都是复合词，后面接一个常用词。

abstract.en: Rings counted on a fresh stump.
abstract.cn: 在新鲜的树桩上数年轮。

abstract.en: A grain that pulls a nail slightly to one side.
abstract.cn: 木纹让钉子微微歪向一边。

abstract.en: Warmth that comes from a wall of old beams.
abstract.cn: 一面旧梁柱墙传来的温度。

examples.en: The old chair is carved from a single block of wood.
examples.cn: 这把旧椅子是用一整块木头雕成的。

examples.en: They gathered dry wood for the fire before nightfall.
examples.cn: 天黑前他们捡好了烧火用的干柴。

examples.en: A path runs through the woods behind the village school.
examples.cn: 一条小路穿过村小学后面的林子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「屋的」——盖屋子用的，正是木材。

root: 古英语 wudu（树；木材），与荷兰语、德语同源；加 -en 得 wooden，加 -y 得 woody。

sensesIntro.en: The material comes first, then the place where it grows, then the part of an object once cut from it, and finally the dull wooden quality.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是材料，再是长材料的地方，接着是用它削成的部件，最后是发闷的木质质感。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rings counted on a freshly cut stump.
core.cn: 核心意象：在刚锯开的树桩上数年轮。

branches.en: The material branch: a table of old oak wood.
branches.cn: 材料分支：老橡木做的桌子。

branches.en: The place branch: a walk through the woods at dusk.
branches.cn: 地方分支：黄昏穿过林子。

branches.en: The club branch: a wooden head striking the ball.
branches.cn: 球杆分支：木制杆头击球。

branches.en: The sound branch: the wood section of an orchestra.
branches.cn: 声音分支：乐团的木管声部。

branches.en: The quality branch: wood as a word for stiffness and dullness.
branches.cn: 质感分支：wood 用来形容僵硬与发闷。

intro.en: Wood is a bare native stem; the endings -en and -y are what turn the material into adjectives.
intro.cn: wood 是一个不带词缀的本土词干；把材料变成形容词的是 -en 与 -y 两个词尾。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic with no Latin ancestor; the Latin words below name the same material from another branch.

definition_zh: 争论；论证；说服
definition_en: to disagree in words, or to give reasons for an opinion, or to persuade someone with reasons
core_image: 两个男孩指着最后一个座位争执
scene: 两个男孩为了最后一个座位争了起来，声音越来越高。 The two boys argued about the last seat.
sceneCN: 这里 argued 是「争论」（第 1 个义项：用言语争执）；句意为两个男孩为最后一个座位争吵。

senses.title: To disagree in words
senses.definition: to speak against someone because you disagree
senses.definitionCN: 因意见不同而用言语对抗
senses.example: The two boys argued about the last seat.
senses.exampleCN: 两个男孩为最后一个座位争吵。
senses.why: Two people pressing opposite views in words gives the first sense of the verb.
senses.whyCN: 两个人用话语各推一边，就是这个词的第一义。

senses.title: To give reasons for an opinion
senses.definition: to give reasons to show that an opinion is right
senses.definitionCN: 给出理由以说明某个看法是对的
senses.example: She argued that the plan was too costly.
senses.exampleCN: 她论证说这个计划成本太高。
senses.why: Making a matter clear by reasons is the older Latin sense, kept in the arguing of a case.
senses.whyCN: 用理由把事情说清是更早的拉丁义，保留在「论证」这个用法里。

senses.title: To persuade with reasons
senses.definition: to persuade someone to do something by giving reasons
senses.definitionCN: 通过讲理由劝人做某事
senses.example: He argued her into joining the team.
senses.exampleCN: 他说服她加入了队伍。
senses.why: The same reasons aimed at changing a mind become the act of persuading.
senses.whyCN: 同样的理由用来改变别人的想法，就成了说服。

intro.en: The recorded history of argue is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 argue 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: Arguere meant to make clear or to prove.
items.cn: arguere 意为使其清楚或证明。

items.en: Argumentum meant a proof or a reason.
items.cn: argumentum 意为证明或理由。

items.en: Old French shaped it into arguer, to dispute.
items.cn: 古法语把它变成 arguer，意为争辩。

items.en: English used argue for both dispute and proof.
items.cn: 英语十四世纪用 argue 兼指争执与证明。

items.en: Today it also covers persuading someone by reasons.
items.cn: 今天它也涵盖用理由说服他人。

note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收意义相近的词。

entries.definitionCN: 动词的第三人称单数形式。

entries.definition: The noun for a dispute or a reason.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指争执或理由。

entries.definition: The adjective for something open to debate.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指可争辩的。

entries.definition: It stresses an angry personal dispute.
entries.definitionCN: 强调人与人之间愤怒的争吵。

entries.definition: A more formal word for a disagreement.
entries.definitionCN: 更正式的说法，指意见分歧。

entries.definition: It stresses a formal exchange of reasons.
entries.definitionCN: 强调正式的意见交锋。

normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的词形、真实的词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: The Latin arguere meant to make clear: arguing is putting reasons in plain view.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 arguere 意为使其清楚：argue 就是把理由摆到明处。

normal.en: The same family also gives argument and arguable.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 argument 与 arguable。

normal.en: It often appears in the phrase argue with.
normal.cn: 它常出现在「与……争论」这个搭配里。

normal.en: Spell it as it sounds: keep every letter of argue in order.
normal.cn: 按读音拼写：把 argue 的每个字母按顺序保留。

normal.cn: 当你想表达「争论」时用它。

definition_zh: 指示；说明；教学
definition_en: a direction telling you what to do, or the act of teaching someone
core_image: 说明书上印着一步一步的箭头
scene: 桌面上摊着新家具的装配图。 Follow the instructions before you plug it in.
sceneCN: 这里 instruction 是「指示」（第 1 个义项：告诉你做什么的说明）；句意：插电前请先看说明书。

derivatives.zh: instruction 的动词基，义为「指示；教导」
instruct 加施动者后缀，义为「教员；指导员」
instruction 加形容词后缀，义为「教学的」

senses.title: A direction to act
senses.definition: an order or direction telling someone what to do
senses.definitionCN: 告诉某人做什么的命令或指示
senses.example: We waited for instructions from the office.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在等办公室的指示。
senses.why: An arrow on the page points at your hands.
senses.whyCN: 纸上的箭头指向你的双手。

senses.title: Steps for using something
senses.definition: written steps explaining how to use or make something
senses.definitionCN: 说明如何使用或制作的成文步骤
senses.example: Read the assembly instructions first.
senses.exampleCN: 先读装配说明。
senses.why: The arrows form a small staircase of steps.
senses.whyCN: 箭头连成小小的阶梯。

senses.title: The act of teaching
senses.definition: the act or process of teaching knowledge or skills
senses.definitionCN: 传授知识或技能的行为
senses.example: Instruction in the pool begins Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 泳池教学周一开始。
senses.why: The arrow bends into a teacher's finger.
senses.whyCN: 箭头弯成了老师的手指。

senses.title: Computer commands
senses.definition: a single command a computer can perform
senses.definitionCN: 计算机可执行的一条命令
senses.example: The chip runs millions of instructions per second.
senses.exampleCN: 芯片每秒执行数百万条指令。
senses.why: The arrow is etched into silicon.
senses.whyCN: 箭头被刻进了硅片。

intro.en: Instruction comes from Latin instruere, to build into or pile up for teaching, from in- (in) and struere (to build). Teaching was seen as building knowledge into a person.
intro.cn: instruction 来自拉丁语 instruere「砌入、堆叠以教导」，由 in-「在内」+ struere「建造」构成；教学被视为把知识砌进人心里。

items.en: Latin struere meant to build up, the same root as structure.
items.cn: 拉丁语 struere 意为垒建，与 structure 同根。

items.en: in- plus struere formed instruere: to build in, to educate.
items.cn: in- 加 struere 构成 instruere：砌入，引申为教育。

items.en: Latin instructio named the act of equipping with knowledge.
items.cn: 拉丁语 instructio 指以知识装备人的行为。

items.en: Old French instruction passed the word to English.
items.cn: 古法语 instruction 把词传给英语。

items.en: Middle English instruccioun covered teaching and orders alike.
items.cn: 中古英语 instruccioun 兼指教学与命令。

items.en: Modern English added the printed manual and the computer command.
items.cn: 现代英语新增了印刷说明与计算机指令两义。

note.cn: 形近组收录「建造」词根词族；词义组比较命令与教学类词。

entries.definitionCN: 授课这项工作。

sceneCN: 这里 memory 指「唤起过往经历的能力」（第 1 个义项：把过去的片段重新调出）；句意为消毒水的气味让她立刻回到多年前陪护家人的那个下午。图中可辨识物件：医院走廊、消毒水瓶、长椅、被唤起的时间线；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 记忆；记忆力；回忆；纪念；计算机内存

senses.title: The ability to remember
senses.definition: the faculty by which information and past experiences are stored and recalled
senses.definitionCN: 储存并调取信息与过往经历的能力
senses.example: The smell of disinfectant brings back that afternoon at once.
senses.exampleCN: 消毒水的气味立刻把她带回那个下午。
senses.why: memory names a capacity before it names any particular content: the cupboard exists before the things put in it.
senses.whyCN: memory 先命名一种能力，再命名具体内容：柜子先存在，东西才放进去。

senses.title: A remembered event
senses.definition: a particular past event that one can recall
senses.definitionCN: 能够回想起来的一件具体往事
senses.example: Her earliest memory is of a blue door.
senses.exampleCN: 她最早的记忆是一扇蓝色的门。
senses.why: the mass noun becomes countable when a single episode is pulled out of the store and held up.
senses.whyCN: 当单个片段被从库房里取出并举起时，不可数名词就变成可数。

senses.title: The content stored
senses.definition: the information or impression retained about something
senses.definitionCN: 关于某事物所保留的信息或印象
senses.example: His memory of the route was better than the map.
senses.exampleCN: 他对路线的记忆比地图还准。
senses.why: what is stored is not the event but a trace of it, which is why memory can be accurate and wrong at the same time.
senses.whyCN: 被储存的不是事件本身，而是事件的痕迹；因此记忆可以既准确又出错。

senses.title: Remembrance and commemoration
senses.definition: the keeping of someone or something in respectful remembrance
senses.definitionCN: 以敬意把某人或某事留在怀念中
senses.example: A bench was placed in memory of the teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 一张长椅被安放以纪念这位老师。
senses.why: the word widens from an individual's store to a community's shared keeping, and the phrase in memory of marks that shift.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从个人的储存扩展到群体的共同保存；「为纪念……」这一短语标记了这种转移。

senses.title: Reputation after death
senses.definition: the way a person is remembered by later generations
senses.definitionCN: 后人对某人的记忆与评价
senses.example: The engineer left a memory of honesty.
senses.exampleCN: 这位工程师留下了诚实的名声。
senses.why: if memory is what survives, then a person's memory is the part of them that outlives them.
senses.whyCN: 如果 memory 是留存下来的东西，那么一个人的 memory 就是比他活得更久的那部分。

senses.title: Computer memory
senses.definition: the electronic storage in a computer that holds data and programs for immediate use
senses.definitionCN: 计算机中存放数据与程序以供即时使用的电子存储
senses.example: The program needs more memory than the laptop has.
senses.exampleCN: 这个程序需要的内存超过这台笔记本的容量。
senses.why: the machine metaphor is literal: data is put in, kept, and taken out, exactly like a remembered thing.
senses.whyCN: 机器的比喻是字面的：数据被放入、保存、取出，和记住的东西完全一样。

senses.title: Storage capacity
senses.definition: the amount of data a device or medium can hold
senses.definitionCN: 设备或介质能够容纳的数据量
senses.example: The phone has sixty-four gigabytes of memory.
senses.exampleCN: 这部手机有六十四吉字节的存储。
senses.why: once storage is a place, it can be measured like shelf space, so the noun shifts from the place to its size.
senses.whyCN: 存储一旦成为场所，就能像货架空间那样被计量，于是名词从场所转为容量。

senses.title: A memorial object or rite
senses.definition: an object, day or ceremony that keeps someone or something in mind
senses.definitionCN: 把某人或某事留在心上的物品、日子或仪式
senses.example: The village holds a memory ceremony every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村庄每年春天举行纪念仪式。
senses.why: a memorial is memory externalized, made visible so that forgetting becomes harder.
senses.whyCN: 纪念物是记忆的外化，被做成看得见的东西，使遗忘更困难。

senses.title: A type of memory system
senses.definition: a named subsystem such as working, short-term or long-term memory
senses.definitionCN: 被命名的子系统，如工作记忆、短时记忆或长时记忆
senses.example: Working memory holds a phone number just long enough to dial.
senses.exampleCN: 工作记忆把电话号码保留到拨完为止。
senses.why: research splits the cupboard into compartments, and each compartment inherits the same word.
senses.whyCN: 研究把柜子分成隔间，每个隔间都继承同一个词。

intro.en: Memory comes from Latin memoria, from memor 'mindful', and reached English through Old French. The computing sense is twentieth-century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: memory 来自拉丁 memoria，源自 memor「记得的」，经古法语进入英语。计算义是 20 世纪的延伸。年代为约数。

items.en: Memor was an adjective meaning 'mindful, remembering'; it described a person who keeps something in mind.
items.cn: memor 是形容词，意为「记得的、留心的」，描述把某事放在心上的人。

items.en: Memoria 'memory, remembrance, the faculty of remembering' was built on memor and named both the capacity and its content.
items.cn: memoria「记忆、怀念、记忆力」由 memor 构成，同时命名能力与内容。

items.en: Old French memorie carried the word into English in the thirteenth century; the ending settled as -y.
items.cn: 古法语 memorie 在 13 世纪把词带入英语；词尾最终固定为 -y。

items.en: The deeper root is reconstructed as *men- 'to think', also present in mind and in Greek mnēmē 'memory'.
items.cn: 更早的词根被重构为 *men-「思考」，也出现在英语的「心智」一词与希腊语 mnēmē「记忆」中。

items.en: Memory in the machine sense dates from the 1940s, when early computers stored instructions electronically.
items.cn: 机器义的 memory 形成于 20 世纪 40 年代，当时早期计算机以电子方式存储指令。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the exact first English use of the computing sense is not fixed, and the pre-Latin history of memor is reconstructed rather than directly attested.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：计算义的最早英语用法没有确切年代；memor 在拉丁语之前的历史属于重构，而非直接书证。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same memor family that are easily swapped; group two holds words about bringing the past back.
note.cn: 第一组是同一 memor 词族里容易混用的词；第二组是关于把过去重新带回的词。

entries.definition: To commit something to memory deliberately; memory is the store, memorize is the act of putting something in.
entries.definitionCN: 有意把某物记入记忆；memory 是库房，memorize 是放入的动作。

entries.definition: Something built or held to remember a person or event; it externalizes memory rather than naming the faculty.
entries.definitionCN: 为纪念某人或某事而建或举行的东西；把记忆外化，而非命名能力。

entries.definition: Worthy of being remembered; it judges the content, while memory names the container.
entries.definitionCN: 值得记住的；评判内容，而 memory 命名容器。

entries.definition: A note made so that something will not be forgotten; Latin memorare 'to mention' supplies it, not the noun memory directly.
entries.definitionCN: 为防止遗忘而写的备忘；来自拉丁 memorare「提及」，并非直接由名词 memory 派生。

entries.definition: The act of bringing something back to mind; memory is the store, recall is the hand that reaches in.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物重新带回心头的动作；memory 是库房，recall 是伸进去的手。

entries.definition: The process of piecing a past scene together; it often implies effort and partial reconstruction.
entries.definitionCN: 把过去场景一块块拼回来的过程；常暗示费力与部分重建。

entries.definition: The act of keeping someone in mind, often with ceremony; it leans toward commemoration rather than storage.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人留在心上的行为，常伴仪式；偏向纪念而非储存。

entries.definition: The degree to which learned material remains available over time; it measures memory's durability.
entries.definitionCN: 所学材料随时间保留的程度；衡量记忆的持久性。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: memor 'mindful' + -y gives memory; the same stem runs through memorize, memorial and memorable.
normal.cn: memor「记得的」+ -y 构成 memory；同一词干贯穿 memorize、memorial 与 memorable。

normal.en: The family runs memorize, memorization, memorial, memorable and remembrance.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 memorize、memorization、memorial、memorable 与 remembrance。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: from memory, in memory of, working memory, memory loss.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：凭记忆、为纪念、工作记忆、记忆丧失。

normal.en: In computing, memory is a place; in psychology, it is both a place and a capacity.
normal.cn: 在计算机领域，memory 是场所；在心理学中，它既是场所也是能力。

normal.en: Memory is the cupboard, recall is the act of opening it.
normal.cn: memory 是柜子，recall 是打开柜子的动作。

abstract.en: Picture a dark warehouse where every box is labelled by date.
abstract.cn: 想象一座昏暗的库房，每个箱子都按日期贴标签。

abstract.en: Picture a smell that opens a door you did not know was there.
abstract.cn: 想象一种气味打开了一扇你不知道存在的门。

abstract.en: Picture a stone bench that keeps saying one name without sound.
abstract.cn: 想象一张石凳无声地反复说着一个名字。

examples.en: He recited the poem from memory.
examples.cn: 他凭记忆背诵了这首诗。

examples.en: The garden was planted in memory of her mother.
examples.cn: 这座花园是为纪念她母亲而种的。

examples.en: The update needs more memory than the old tablet has.
examples.cn: 这次更新需要的内存超过旧平板电脑的容量。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「没魔力」——记得住不是因为魔力，而是因为反复回看 → 记忆

root: 拉丁 memoria「记忆」← memor「记得的」；更早可重构为印欧语 *men-「思考」，与 mind、希腊语 mnēmē 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one cupboard: the capacity, one recalled event, the stored content, communal keeping, posthumous reputation, the machine's store, its size, the visible memorial and the named subsystem.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一间库房展开：能力、一段回忆、所存内容、共同保存、身后名声、机器存储、容量、可见的纪念物，以及被命名的子系统。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a numbered store from which a past piece is fetched on demand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座编号库房，按需把过去的片段取出。

branches.en: THE STORE AND ITS PIECES: capacity, one event, and the trace that remains.
branches.cn: 库房与片段：能力、单件往事，以及留下的痕迹。

branches.en: OUTWARD KEEPING: memory leaves the head as a ceremony or a bench.
branches.cn: 向外的保存：记忆以仪式或长椅的形式离开脑袋。

branches.en: AFTER LIFE: what survives of a person is precisely their memory in others.
branches.cn: 身后：一个人留下来的，正是他在别人心中的记忆。

branches.en: MACHINE: the same cupboard is built in silicon and then measured in gigabytes.
branches.cn: 机器：同一间库房用硅造出来，再以吉字节计量。

branches.en: COMPARTMENTS: research divides the cupboard and names each shelf.
branches.cn: 隔间：研究把柜子分开，并给每层架子命名。

intro.en: Memory is a Latin adjective turned noun: memor plus -y. The same stem builds a large family of verbs, adjectives and monuments.
intro.cn: memory 是拉丁形容词变来的名词：memor 加 -y。同一词干构成一大批动词、形容词与纪念物。

latinIntro.en: Latin memor 'mindful' gives memoria and memorare; English draws memory, memorize, memorial, memorable and remembrance from this line.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 memor「记得的」生成 memoria 与 memorare；英语由此得到 memory、memorize、memorial、memorable 与 remembrance。

items.example: Memor is the adjective behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: memor 是整个词族背后的形容词。

items.example: The suffix turns the adjective into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成名词。

items.example: Memoria named both the power and its content.
items.exampleCN: memoria 同时命名能力与内容。

items.meaning: the faculty or content of remembering
items.example: Memory can be trained but not enlarged at will.
items.exampleCN: 记忆可以训练，却不能随意扩容。

items.meaning: the act of committing to memory
a thing that keeps a person in mind
items.exampleCN: 纪念碑上列出了每个名字。

items.meaning: to honour by keeping in memory
items.exampleCN: 这块铭牌纪念那次救援。
